preset.description: A saw-shaped stack of partials whose Tilt is swept by a slow LFO, from dark and woolly to bright and ringing, with no filter involved. Reduce Partials for a rounder tone or push Tilt up for an organ-like glare.
Odd/Even is pulled to the odd side so only the 1st, 3rd, 5th partials sound: a hollow, reedy tone. Move Odd/Even through zero to bring back the even partials and watch the reed turn into a full saw.

A flat spectrum with Stretch pushing the partials apart gives inharmonic, bell-like tones, and each trigger restarts a decay that makes the high partials die first. Change Stretch for a metallic or glassy family, or Decay for longer ringing.
A slow chord line played by a comb-notched spectrum with a wide chorus, giving a shimmering, voice-like pad. Change Comb Spacing to move the notches or raise Chorus for a bigger, more unstable cloud.

patches.name: Additive Osc: Odd and Even Split

preset.description: The odd-partial and even-partial outputs go to separate mixer channels whose pans drift in opposite directions, so the two halves of one tone circle each other. Mute one channel to hear its half alone.

panels.name: Additive Osc: Odd and Even Split

controls.text: Additive Osc: Odd and Even Split

preset.description: Two ADSRs share each note: one shapes the volume, the other sweeps a low-pass filter from open to closed, so every note starts bright and darkens. Shorten Decay for staccato plucks, or raise Sustain to let the notes ring.
With a long Attack and a long Release, each held note rises out of silence and melts away over the next one, so the chords seem to breathe. Try a shorter Attack to turn the pad into a soft organ.

The sequencer sends a different velocity with every note into the ADSR, and Vel Amount decides how much it matters: soft notes are quiet and mellow, accented ones loud and bright. Set Vel Amount to zero and the phrase goes flat.

A fast Attack with a medium Decay and a high Sustain gives the bass a tight thump that then holds its note until the gate closes. Lower Sustain for a plucked bass, lengthen Release to let notes blur into each other.

When each note's envelope finishes, its End output fires a rim shot, so the percussion trails after the melody at a distance set by Decay and Release. Lengthen the Release and the echo hits arrive later.

A four-bar progression of held chords is broken into a plucked run that climbs through two octaves and starts over. Try Pattern, Octaves and Rate on the Arpeggiator to turn the same chords into a different tune.

The Arpeggiator climbs and falls over three octaves in triplet eighths with a touch of Swing, giving a rolling, harp-like figure behind a slow chord change. Change Rate to 1/8 or 1/16 for straight timing.

The pattern is Random over four octaves at sixteenth notes, so the chord tones scatter into a glittery, never-quite-repeating line over a beat. The Seed picks the shuffle: change it for a different sequence.

A low saw bass takes the outside notes first and works inwards, the Converge pattern over two octaves, with a bit of Swing under a driving beat. Try Diverge for the reverse, or Down for a falling line.

A downward arpeggio at quarter-note speed with a short Gate Length turns each chord into a few soft bell strikes that fade into a long reverb. Increase Rate to eighth notes for a busier shimmer, or Latch to keep a chord ringing.

One slow LFO enters two rows of the Attenuverter, one scaled +1 and one -1, and they open the left filter while closing the right one, so the arpeggio seems to travel across the stereo field. Change the scale of either row to unbalance the sweep.

With nothing patched in, each Attenuverter row is a constant set by its Offset: row 1 transposes the sequencer up a fourth and row 2 holds the filter at a fixed opening. Turn Offset 1 to change key while the music plays.

Three unrelated modulators, a slow sine, a triangle and a smooth random line, go into three rows and meet at the Sum output, which sweeps the filter along a path that rarely repeats. Change a row's scale to give one modulator more say.

A triangle LFO is doubled by the row's Scale and hard-clipped, so the filter spends most of the time fully open or fully closed and only moves quickly in between. Set Clip to Off or Soft to round the sweep, or lower Scale to reduce the effect.

A kick's envelope goes through a row set to scale -1 with offset +1, turning a short burst into a short dip, and that dip pumps the volume of a chord pad on every beat. Lower the negative Scale for a gentler duck.
Drums, a bass, a chord line and a lead each sit on their own channel with their own level and pan: bass in the middle, chords left, lead right. Pull a Level down or move a Pan to rebalance the band.

Each channel's Send feeds one reverb whose output returns on Return: the lead is awash in it, the bass stays dry. Raise Send 1 for more space, and switch Send Point to Pre-Fader to keep the reverb when a channel's Level is turned down.

Mute inputs are fed from drum-grid tracks, so the hats, the chord stabs and the bass drop in and out of the mix on their own in a repeating pattern. Switch a Solo on to isolate one part, or turn a Mute on by hand.

All four channels are driven hot, well above 0 dB, and the built-in Limiter holds the master bus below full scale, giving a loud, dense and slightly pumping sound. Turn the Limiter setting off to hear how far past clipping the inputs are, and lower Master to keep it safe.

Two arpeggios are panned hard left and hard right with wide detune, then summed to the middle by the Mono setting: a quick way to hear what happens to a wide mix on a single speaker. Switch Mono off to open them back out, or change the Pan values.

A ring of sixteen cells grows under rule 30 from a single seed cell; the read head sweeps round the ring, so the lit cells become notes and the dark ones rests. Change Rule (90 mirrors itself, 110 drifts) or raise Interference to nudge the pattern off its course; Reset returns to the seed.

An 8 by 8 wrapping world: colonies grow, collide and die. Gate and Pitch play a bell-like lead, every birth of a cell triggers a soft hat, and Density, how alive the grid is, opens a filter. Try the other Grid Rule choices, or raise Density for a crowded start.

A frozen eight-note loop plays on the left and is patched into the chain's Learn input; the chain on the right listens, adds the moves it hears to its transition table and improvises in the same style. Turn Learn down to hear the plain, stepwise table, or open the module to edit the table by hand.

A walker with four turn rules roams an 8 by 8 wrapping grid; it plays a note whenever it steps onto a marked cell and fires Birth when it lays a fresh mark. Gate drives a bass, Birth drives hats and a snare, and the walker's route repeats until Interference nudges it somewhere new.

A phrase rewrites itself each time it ends, growing longer and then starting over. A slow square LFO patched into Rewind pulls the system four generations back every few seconds, so the phrase keeps returning to something it has played, but never exactly the same way. Change Rewind By or the Rules choice.

Two high carriers beat against each other and a slow LFO sweeps Beat, so a pure tone glides down into a throbbing pulse and back. Turn Drift up for a wandering, unstable tone or move Beat by hand for a held pitch.

The sequencer's pitch is fed to the Pitch input so the heterodyne tone plays a tune, with a gentle envelope for each note. Change Carrier to shift the character, or raise Fine to detune the whole line.

A slow LFO raises Pull so the two carriers try to lock: the tone stutters, drops into pulses and jumps into pitch as they catch each other. Move Pull and Detector by hand to hear the stutter appear and disappear.

A low heterodyne bass under a drum loop: each sequencer note retunes the pair through Pitch and an envelope shapes it, with the Diode mixer adding grit. Try the Range setting at ±20 Hz or ±2 kHz and move Beat to change how deep it sits.

The Mixer setting on Overdriven adds harmonics and sidebands to the beat tone, and Drift keeps it alive and slightly unstable. Compare Ideal, Diode and Overdriven to hear the same beat with three characters.
Crush mode grabs sixteenth-note pieces of a drum loop and repeats them, with pitch steps by octave and a little corruption. Raise Chance for a busier mess, or lower Repeats for a gentler stutter.
Dropout mode punches holes into an arpeggio, as if the signal kept losing contact. Move Chance for more or fewer gaps, Time for the length of each hole, and try another Seed.

Fold mode with Bend steps set to Fifths + octaves repeats short pieces of a slow melody a fifth or an octave away, so the glitches stay musical. Switch Bend Steps to Free for wild slides, or raise Bend Var.

Shuffle mode with Slice cuts a swung beat into small pieces and reorders them, so the groove is always almost the same and never quite. Turn Slice down for longer chunks, or Chance up for more reshuffling.
Smear mode melts a chord arpeggio together while a square LFO holds Freeze for a bar at a time, looping one grain until the gate lets go. Try the LFO's rate, or latch Freeze on and off by hand.

A dark, muffled saw riff plays on its own; hold the Button and its Gate output opens an envelope that sweeps the filter wide open, then lets it fall back when you let go. Try the Toggle mode to latch the bright sound.

A warm pad-like line carries the patch; click the Button in Toggle mode and a second, bell-like line fades in on top and stays until you click again. Switch Mode to Momentary to bring the bells in only while you hold it.

A bass line and a half-time beat play by themselves; every press of the Button sends a Trigger to a clap, so you add hand claps by tapping it in time. The Trigger fires on the press, not on the release, and its Gate output would stay high while you hold.

Press and hold the Button, then let go: its Release output fires a long crash cymbal at the moment you lift your finger, like a drum-fill finish. Use the Trigger output on the same Button to hit the cymbal on the way down instead.

In Toggle mode the Button's Toggle output latches the reverb's Freeze input: click it while a note is ringing and the tail is held as an endless chord under the following notes. Click again to let the room empty.

A grid of eight columns and two rows: the X playhead runs along a row every sixteenth and Y drops to the second row when it reaches the end, so a sixteen-note riff in G Dorian comes out in order. Change Rows to 1 for a short loop, or edit a cell's pitch in the view.

Both playheads bounce back and forth over a 6 × 4 patch of the grid, X on the eighths and Y once a bar, so a marimba line keeps reversing and the long path takes ages to repeat. Set the directions to Forward for a plain scan, or Random to lose the pattern.

Every cell also stores a Mod value, and here the Mod output opens the filter of an acid bass, so each step has its own brightness: notes with a high Mod bite, low ones stay dark. Edit the Mod of a cell or turn Mod Slew up to smear the changes.

Cartesian mode: no clocks, two slow LFOs steer the X and Y inputs across a full 8 × 8 grid of Lydian notes, and a note sounds whenever the crosshair enters a new cell. Move X and Y yourself, or change the LFO rates to wander faster.

X runs backward through a 5 × 3 grid, and the Row End and Grid End triggers play the drums: a hat each time a row finishes, a kick and clap when the whole grid has been walked. Change Columns or Rows and the drum accents move with the melody.

A random wander is drawn onto four bars of paper, and the strip is read backwards to sweep a filter over a bass line, so the sweeps are a reversed memory of the pen's line. Set Replay Speed to 1 for the forward path, or draw on the paper yourself.

Pen and replay run on free paper: the line a random source draws is read back at half speed, so a second voice bends its pitch along a slower, stretched copy of what the first one is doing. Try Replay Speed 2 or Paper Speed to change how the two relate.

A square wave goes in, but the sprung pen overshoots and wobbles round every edge, and that ringing line opens and closes a filter on a bass line. Raise Damping to calm the pen, or Friction to make it stick in steps.

The pen records the loudness of a drum loop, as a level recorder would, and the strip replays at double speed to open a filter on a pad twice as often as the drums hit. Change Detector to Peak or Log dB, or put the Replay Speed back to 1.

Every half bar the LFO puts a mark on the paper, and the replay head, shifted by Offset, fires a snare each time it passes a mark: a rhythm that runs slightly out of step with the beat. Change Offset to slide the hits, or Replay Speed for another pattern.

A slow bass line plays the root and Chord Osc stacks a minor seventh on it in the Open voicing, with a little Detune, wide Stereo and Glide so each chord melts into the next. Try other Chord types, change Voicing, or push Inversion up and down to hear the same chord from a different bass note.

patches.name: Chord Osc: Chords From a Melody

preset.description: In Scale mode every note of a simple melody becomes the diatonic chord on that scale degree: major, minor and diminished triads appear by themselves in C major. The melody's trigger is patched into Latch so chords change exactly on the step. Change Scale or Root to re-colour the tune, or set the stack to Seventh.

panels.name: Chord Osc: Chords From a Melody

controls.text: Chord Osc: Chords From a Melody

preset.description: One Chord Osc is two instruments: its Root output, filtered and sub-heavy, is the bassline, and the chord itself plays short offbeat stabs on top (Root Level lowered so they do not double the bass). Try Dominant 9 or Minor add9 in Chord, or open the stab filter.

The four Pitch outputs carry the chord tones from low to high; a Switch steps through them every sixteenth to play an arpeggio on a separate oscillator that always follows the chord. The pad underneath plays the whole chord. Change the Chord, or the Inversion, and the arpeggio changes with it.

Five voices stacked in fourths with the Wide voicing, near-sine waves and slow Detune make a cool, open sound with no clear major or minor. A slow LFO sweeps the Inversion, so the bass note of the chord keeps changing. Switch Chord to Sus2 or Add9 for a warmer cloud.

A slow root line goes into the Chord Quantizer, which stacks each root as a minor seventh over four voices; the four oscillators swell into a lush, moving pad. Try Chord on Dominant 9 or Sus4, or Voicing on Spread for a wider sound.

Rhythmic triad stabs follow a four-chord loop, and Voice Leading chooses the inversion that moves least, so the top voice glides instead of jumping. Turn Voice Leading Off to hear every chord land in root position.

Instead of thirds, each chord is stacked in fourths and spread wide: an open, floating sound that suits slow, bell-like notes. Try Inversion or Range to move the stack, or Chord to Fifth for a hollow drone.

In Diatonic mode a melody in C major is harmonised note by note: each pitch becomes the root of the right triad for the scale, major on some steps, minor on others. Change the Stack to Seventh, or the setting Scale to Dorian.

patches.name: Chord Quantizer: Chords into an Arpeggio

preset.description: The Notes output of the Chord Quantizer holds each chord while an Arpeggiator breaks it into a running pattern for a single pluck voice. Change the chord, then the Arpeggiator's Pattern or Octaves, to reshape the same harmony.

panels.name: Chord Quantizer: Chords into an Arpeggio

controls.text: Chord Quantizer: Chords into an Arpeggio

preset.description: A mono saw pad is turned into a wide, slowly shimmering ensemble by the Chorus: slow Rate, plenty of Depth and full Spread. Raise Rate for a faster wobble or lower Spread to hear the stereo image collapse.

In Flanger mode with strong Feedback and a short Delay, a beat and a hat-heavy groove get a slow jet-engine sweep through every sound. Lower Feedback for a mild swirl or raise Depth for a wider sweep.
A bright pluck melody gets a gentle Chorus with a short Delay and small Depth: it thickens like a doubled instrument without obvious wobble. Increase Depth to push it toward a seasick vibrato.

With Mix at 100 % only the moving delay is heard, which wobbles the pitch like a warped tape: a fast Rate gives vibrato, a slow one a seasick drift. Lower Mix to blend the dry sound back in as a chorus.

A flanger with negative Feedback hollows out a sustained saw, and an LFO slowly moves its Delay, so the tone sweeps through metallic, hollow resonances. Flip Feedback positive for a brighter, ringing comb.

One 16th-note clock is cut into /2, /3, /5, /8 and /16: hats on the fast outputs, a kick every eight steps, a rim every three and a cowbell every five, so the layers drift in and out of line. Edit any Div knob to retune a layer; they all realign on the downbeat of the 16-step cycle.

Four outputs divide an eighth-note clock by 3, 4, 5 and 7 and each rings a different bell tone, so a calm major pentatonic cluster slowly rearranges itself. Change one Div by a single step and the whole pattern shifts.

Powers of two (/1, /2, /4, /8) in Trigger mode play a kick, snare, hat and bass in a fixed, regular pattern, a bit like the bits of a counter. Change Base to 1/8T for a rolling feel, or set Realign to 4 bars to snap the layers back together on a longer cycle.

With Output set to Gate and Gate Length on Division, the slow outputs (/16, /24, /32 and /48) hold long gates that swell three chord tones in and out at different times. Narrow Width shortens the swells; try Gate Length = Base Step for short blips instead.

patches.name: Clock Div: Clocks for Two Melodies

preset.description: Two Step Sequencers have no clock of their own: one takes /2 and one takes /3 of the divider, so an 8-note arpeggio and a 5-note bass line run at different speeds and phase against each other. Move a Div knob to speed one of them up or down.

panels.name: Clock Div: Clocks for Two Melodies

controls.text: Clock Div: Clocks for Two Melodies

preset.description: One quarter-note clock becomes a kick on the beat, hats at four per beat, a rim at 3/2 and a cowbell at 5/4: the last two drift against the kick and meet it again every few beats. Change a Ratio knob and the layer re-tunes.

Swing on a Clock Mult output moves only the in-between ticks: the kick and the snare sit on the beat while the sixteenth hats lean late. Turn Swing up for a harder shuffle, Humanize for a looser hand, or raise Skip 3 for fewer ghost hats.

patches.name: Clock Mult: Clock for a Line

preset.description: A Step Sequencer has no clock of its own: it takes Out 1 of Clock Mult at four ticks per beat with a late swing, and the bass takes Out 2 at one per beat. Change Ratio 1 to 3 or 3/2 for a different gait; the line follows the multiplier.

panels.name: Clock Mult: Clock for a Line

controls.text: Clock Mult: Clock for a Line

preset.description: Four bell tones ring at 2/3, 3/4, 5/4 and 7/4 of the clock with Skip on the busy ones, so a calm pentatonic cloud never quite repeats. Move one Ratio by a step and the whole constellation shifts.

patches.name: Clock Mult: Chained from a Divider

preset.description: Clock Div turns the 16th grid into a slow beat-rate pulse, and Clock Mult's Clock jack counts those pulses and multiplies them back up: tight at full Phase Lock, and a flywheel that keeps going at zero. Try 3 and 5/4 against the divider's own outputs.

panels.name: Clock Mult: Chained from a Divider

controls.text: Clock Mult: Chained from a Divider

preset.description: Every eighth-note gate is sent either to a kick or to a snare by a fair coin, so the backbeat is never the same twice, over a fixed hat and bass line. Push Probability 1 up for more kicks, or change Seed for a different run of luck.

A steady sixteenth-note stream is split by a loaded coin: four tosses in five give a closed hat and the rest an open one, over a plain kick and clap. Move Probability 1 toward 0.5 for a busier, more open hat line.

Eight eighth-note tosses decide whether a low note or a high note sounds, and Loop makes the same eight outcomes repeat, so a tune made by chance settles into a pattern you can hum. Set Loop to Off and it never repeats; change Seed for another tune.

Once a bar the coin picks one of two pads, an A minor chord or an F major chord; in Latch mode the chosen side stays on until the next toss, so one chord always sounds. Raise Memory 1 and the coin tends to repeat the last result.

With Link set to Opposed, channel 2 always chooses the other side from channel 1: when the first coin sends a gate to the kick, the second sends its gate to the hat, and the other way round. Try Shared to make both coins land together.

A sustained saw pad runs through the Compressor while the kick drum feeds its Key input: every kick pushes the pad down and it swells back between beats. Lower Threshold or lengthen Release for a deeper, slower pump.

A broken beat is flattened with a high Ratio, fast Attack and a lot of Makeup, then blended back with Mix at about half: the room and tails come up while the hits keep their punch. Sweep Mix from 0 to 100 % to hear what the squash adds.
A bass line with wildly different velocities is evened out by an RMS Compressor with a soft Knee, so soft notes sit as firmly as loud ones. Raise Threshold until the quiet notes drop back out again.

The Compressor's Reduction output is a control signal that rises with every kick, and here it also closes a Multi Filter on the pad: the sound ducks and darkens on each hit. Raise the cable amount or lower Threshold for a heavier effect.

Short plucks pass through a very fast, high-ratio Compressor with high Makeup: the tails are pulled up so every note rings on like a held string. Lengthen Release to hear the sustain breathe, or cut Makeup to hear the plain pluck.

A soft sine arpeggio on side A and a bright buzzy line on side B share one Crossfader; a slow LFO on Fade moves between them. Drag Fade by hand, or try the Linear curve and listen for the dip at the middle.

Two different drum loops run at once, a steady four-on-the-floor and a broken pattern, and a square LFO flips the Crossfader between them every two bars. Change the LFO's Sync for faster swaps, or move Fade by hand to blend both beats.

A plucked line is split: side A is the dry signal and side B goes through a long, fully wet reverb. Random values on Fade walk the blend between a close, dry sound and a distant, washed one. Turn Fade by hand to set your own mix.

The same saw line goes through a dark low-pass on A and a bright, resonant high-pass on B, and an envelope on Fade sweeps from one colour to the other on each note. Change either filter's Cutoff to retune the two colours, or the envelope's Decay for a slower change.

Curve is set to Linear: two similar sustained chords are cross-faded back and forth by a triangle LFO, and the sum dips slightly in the middle where an equal-power fade would stay full. Switch Curve to Equal Power to hear the dip disappear.
A plain bass line is pushed into Drive with Tone rolled down to 3 kHz: warm, thick overdrive with the harshest top cut away. Raise Drive for fuzz, or open Tone for a more biting edge.

A broken beat loses bits and sample rate, so the kick turns gritty and the hats turn into digital hiss; Mix keeps some of the clean drum underneath. Push Bits toward 1 for noise, or pull Rate Red. down to restore the highs.
Rate Red. at about 55 % with full 16-bit depth leaves the lead's pitch intact but folds new, glassy partials around it, like an old video-game chip. Sweep Rate Red. slowly while the riff plays.

A slow LFO sweeps Bits from clean to coarse and back on a held pad, so the sound breaks into steps and re-forms in long waves. Change the cable amount for a shallower sweep or move Rate Red. for another kind of breakup.

A four-on-the-floor beat gets near-maximum Drive and 8 bits but only 35 % Mix, so the clean punch stays and the crunch adds weight and fizz around it. Move Mix to find where the grit starts to take over.

A sine, a triangle and a stepped random line are added by the CV Mixer in Sum mode, and the result sweeps the arpeggio's filter in a pattern that takes a long time to come round. Pull a channel's Level to zero to hear its share disappear.

Four smooth random lines are averaged into one gentle, never-settling signal that detunes a two-voice pad, so the chord drifts in and out of tune with itself. Change Mode to Sum for a wilder drift, or raise Master to deepen it.

Two unipolar LFOs at different speeds go into Max mode, which always passes the larger one, so the pad swells whenever either wave rises and the volume rarely falls to silence. Switch to Min to hear it only when both are high.

patches.name: CV Mixer: Min as a Gate Maker

preset.description: Two square LFOs of different lengths go into Min mode, which only stays high while both are high, an AND of the two, and the result opens the envelope on a held chord to cut it into a shifting rhythm. Change either LFO's sync to rewrite the pattern.

panels.name: CV Mixer: Min as a Gate Maker

controls.text: CV Mixer: Min as a Gate Maker

preset.description: Four stepped random lines sit in the four channels and Scan, swept by a slow triangle, fades from one to the next; the result is snapped to a scale to play the oscillator, so the tune walks between four moving lines. Move Scan by hand to pick which channel you hear.

patches.name: CV to MIDI: Filter Sweep Out

preset.description: A slow LFO opens and closes the filter of a plucked line, and the same cable also feeds lane 1 of CV to MIDI, which sends the sweep out as CC 74 (open the Monitor to watch the messages). Change CC 1 to send it as another controller, or narrow Min 1 and Max 1.

panels.name: CV to MIDI: Filter Sweep Out

controls.text: CV to MIDI: Filter Sweep Out

patches.name: CV to MIDI: Envelope as Expression

preset.description: Each note's envelope shapes the filter and is also sent as CC 11 through lane 1, so a hardware synth could breathe with the same contour. Lower Max Rate to thin out the messages, or stretch the envelope's Decay and watch the table fill.

panels.name: CV to MIDI: Envelope as Expression

controls.text: CV to MIDI: Envelope as Expression

patches.name: CV to MIDI: Vibrato in 14 Bit

preset.description: A bipolar LFO bends the pitch a few cents and goes out as CC 1 at 14-bit resolution, so slow movement stays smooth instead of stepping. Switch Resolution back to 7 bit, or Input Range to 0 to +1, and compare the table.

panels.name: CV to MIDI: Vibrato in 14 Bit

controls.text: CV to MIDI: Vibrato in 14 Bit

patches.name: CV to MIDI: Four Moving Controls

preset.description: Four LFOs at different speeds move cutoff, resonance, tone and the reverb, and each is sent on its own lane as CC 74, 71, 91 and 93 on separate channels with their own Min and Max. Drag a lane's Max down to squeeze its range.

panels.name: CV to MIDI: Four Moving Controls

controls.text: CV to MIDI: Four Moving Controls

preset.description: A stepped Random changes the filter on every eighth note and CV to MIDI sends each new level as CC 74: only values that moved are sent, so the table shows one message per step. Turn Smooth up on the Random and the messages arrive in streams.

A slow sequencer line becomes notes through CV to Notes, and the Arpeggiator turns each one into a three-octave run. Change the Arpeggiator's pattern, or raise Velocity on CV to Notes to hit the voice harder.

patches.name: CV to Notes: Gates Become Drums

preset.description: Plain gates from a Drum Grid carry no pitch, so CV to Notes sends its fixed Note: 36 is the kick and 38 the snare to a Drum Notes module that turns General MIDI notes back into hits. Change a Note setting to 42 and the snare becomes a hat.

panels.name: CV to Notes: Gates Become Drums

controls.text: CV to Notes: Gates Become Drums

preset.description: A slow LFO sweeps a Quantizer, whose pitch and gate pass through CV to Notes and out as notes to a Notes to CV voice: nothing sequenced, yet a melody. Change the LFO rate for faster runs, or the Quantizer's scale for another colour.

A bass line from a sequencer is sent as notes by CV to Notes into a Harmony Master, which follows the line and holds a chord around it; four oscillators play its chord tones above. Change the Harmony Master's Quality to dress the same line differently.

patches.name: CV to Notes: Soft and Hard Touch

preset.description: The notes leave CV to Notes with a fixed Velocity, and Notes to CV passes it on to open the filter: a low Velocity gives a mellow pluck, a high one a bright bite. Move the Velocity knob while the line plays.

panels.name: CV to Notes: Soft and Hard Touch

controls.text: CV to Notes: Soft and Hard Touch

preset.description: Six taps pass the signal round a ring, so a sparse melody dissolves into a drifting cloud of repeats. Try Taps, Scatter and Character, or switch Routing to Parallel to hear the ring unravel.
In Parallel routing each tap is a separate echo, locked to a dotted eighth so the taps spread into a rhythm around a bright pluck. Change Sync, Scatter or Taps to re-space the pattern.
Chain routing with a large Reverse amount turns the repeats backwards, so every note swells in before it arrives. Lower Reverse for normal echoes, or raise Jitter to blur the swells.

Mesh routing lets every line feed every other, and a slow LFO sweeps Scatter so the swarm of repeats keeps rearranging itself. Try more Jitter and Character for a rougher texture, or less Feedback to calm it.

A square LFO closes the Freeze gate every few bars, trapping the network's contents as a sustained wash while the melody carries on over it. Change the LFO's Sync, or latch the gate with your own control.
A bright pluck line gets a left echo on a dotted eighth and a right echo on a quarter note, so the repeats weave a rhythm of their own. Change Rate L and Rate R, or raise Feedback for longer trails.
Ping-Pong mode bounces each note from one side to the other in sixteenth steps while the arpeggio itself stays sparse. Switch Mode to Stereo to hear the same echoes stay put, or push Feedback up.

A very short free-time delay of about 80 ms with almost no Feedback thickens the drums into a live-room slap. Try Time L and Time R a few milliseconds apart for width, or lengthen both until it becomes an echo.

High Feedback keeps the echoes spiralling while High Cut slowly closes and opens under an LFO, so each repeat gets darker and then brighter. Edit the LFO rate, or raise Low Cut to thin out the build-up.

Two unrelated short times, 23 ms on the left and 37 ms on the right, fatten a slow pad into a wide stereo cloud with no audible echo. Move the Time knobs a little, or turn on Link L/R and watch the image collapse.

One Dial, set to the middle of its range, opens the cutoff of a dark saw riff. Drag the big knob up and down while it plays to sweep the filter, or raise Smooth to make the knob glide between positions.

With Steps set to 12 the Dial jumps between fixed positions instead of sliding, and it feeds the sequencer's Transpose input so the whole tune moves up and down in whole notes. Set Steps to 0 to get a smooth slide, or change Steps to 5 for coarser jumps.
The Dial rides the Mix knob of a very long reverb behind a slow bell tune: at the bottom you hear the dry notes, at the top only their wash. Move it slowly and listen to the tune sink into the room.

Min is higher than Max, so turning the Dial up closes the filter and eases off the drive while the bass sits on a beat. Swap Min and Max to turn the action around, or narrow them to limit how far the knob can go.

One Dial fans out to three destinations at different strengths: the oscillator shape, the filter cutoff and the delay mix, so a single gesture takes a soft sine pluck to a bright, echoing saw. Change the cable amounts to rebalance the macro.

patches.name: Drum Grid: Four on the Floor

preset.description: A house groove from five of the eight tracks: kick on every beat, clap on two and four, hats on the off-beats. Capital X steps are accents and play louder than x steps; click a step in the grid to cycle off, on and accent.

panels.name: Drum Grid: Four on the Floor

controls.text: Drum Grid: Four on the Floor

preset.description: An LFO sweeping once every four bars feeds the Pattern input, so the grid plays a groove twice, then a busier variation, then a fill with toms, and starts over. Set Switch to Immediate to hear it change mid-bar, or take the cable out and pick slots by hand.

The pattern is only 12 steps long, so the grid wraps after three beats and the groove counts in three, with Swing leaning on the off-steps. Each pattern keeps its own Length: stretch it to 16 in the grid view and the waltz turns into a march.

The grid's Accent output, high only when an X step plays, fires an envelope that opens a filter on a low drone, so every accented hit pumps the pad while the quiet x steps leave it closed. Change the grid's Velocity knob to scale the soft hits.

All eight tracks work across two bars of 12/8 (Rate 1/8T, 24 steps): a kick, two toms, a clave, a cowbell, a clap, shaker hats and a distant cymbal. Mute a track in the grid view to hear how the parts interlock.

Two slow LFOs move X and Y through the map, so the beat drifts from sparse to busy and back without ever repeating exactly. Grab the X and Y knobs yourself to park on a pattern you like; the three Density knobs thin out any spot.

Low Density settings leave a spacious beat with only the strongest hits, and a square LFO holds the Fill input for the last bar of every four. Raise Fill Amount for a bigger fill, or raise a Density knob to bring a drum back in.
Chaos at 55 % swaps in a few random changes every bar, a lively breakbeat that is never quite the same twice. Set Chaos Rate to Frozen, or change the Seed, to lock in a version you like.
Rate 1/16T and a 24-step Length turn the map into a rolling triplet shuffle, with Swing and Accent adding a lazy push on top. Switch Rate back to 1/16 to hear the same map played straight.

patches.name: Drum Map: Notes to Other Drums

preset.description: The Notes output sends the map as note events (Kick Note, Snare Note, Hats Note), and Drum Notes turns them into triggers for a different kit: a ring kick, a clap on the snare note and a cowbell on the hats note. Change the three note settings to move a part to another drum.

panels.name: Drum Map: Notes to Other Drums

controls.text: Drum Map: Notes to Other Drums

preset.description: One sequencer plays kick and snare as General MIDI note numbers, another plays closed and open hats; Drum Notes turns each note into a trigger for the right drum. Edit a step's pitch in the sequencer to move a hit to another drum.

The same note-to-drum routing drives a softer, rounder kit of resonant drums on a swung sixteenth grid, with claps on the backbeat. Change the Swing on the sequencers, or swap a kit voice's Tune, and the pattern keeps its feel.
Toms, a woody rim click, a cowbell and a clap are all played from note numbers: Drum Notes has an output for each. Mute one of the sequencers' steps, or tune the toms down, to open up the groove.
A lazy jazz feel: the ride pattern, a pedal hi-hat, a feathered kick and one crash at the top of the bar, all as note numbers. Try the Cymbal's Voice or Decay, or lengthen the ride's pattern.

Drum Notes also passes each hit's velocity, so the quiet ghost snares between the backbeats really are quiet while the accents bite. Raise or lower a step's velocity in the sequencer and hear the dynamics change.

A buzzy saw drone goes through two band-pass filters pulled apart by Spread, which an LFO moves back and forth: the pair of peaks sounds like a vowel changing from 'oo' to 'ah' and back. Change Spread for a different mouth shape, or the Cutoff for a different voice.

In Serial routing the two filters stack into a steep, resonant low-pass that an envelope snaps open on every note. Raise Spread to make the second stage cut lower or higher than the first, or set Character to Saturating for more grit.

Stereo routing sends the left channel through one filter and the right through the other, with Spread putting their cutoffs apart: a busy arpeggio ends up with a dark side and a bright side, which an LFO swaps over time. Try Link set to Mirror or a negative Spread.
Parallel (F2 inverted) combines a low-pass and an inverted copy, carving a moving hole out of a wide chord. Move Cutoff slowly to sweep the gap, or change Balance to favour one side.

A drum loop runs through a driven Dual Filter in Serial mode with Mode 1 and Mode 2 at opposite ends, so lows and highs are both trimmed into a narrow band that opens with a slow LFO. Turn up Drive or Mix to push it harder.

Oscillator B frequency-modulates A while an envelope opens FM Depth and Fold on every note: each note starts bright and metallic and settles to a clearer tone. Change Tune B to pick different FM ratios, or raise Fold for more edge.
A is hard-synced to B and the Sync amount is swept by a slow ramp, so the tone tears from a clean saw into a growling, harmonic-rich buzz. Turn Sync by hand to stop the sweep where you like it.

Two softly detuned cores with Drift and Width turned up make a slowly moving stereo pad, with a hint of Fold from a slow LFO. Raise Drift for more instability or pull Tune B further from A for a thicker chord.

The Ring output multiplies A and B, giving clangorous, bell-like sidebands that die away with each note. Tune B moves the bell from soft and hollow to harsh and tuneless; choose a fifth or a tritone to hear the difference.

A low note from both cores is driven into the wavefolder; Fold rides a slow LFO and Symmetry shifts the odd and even folds, so the bass flips between mellow and snarling. Try the Exponential FM Mode or a different Symmetry for other growls.

A plucked bass line is followed by the Envelope Follower, and the result opens a resonant filter on every note, so the tone speaks with the playing. Try a longer Release for a lazier wah, or more Gain for a wider sweep.

The kick drum is followed and its Inverted output closes a VCA on a sustained pad, so the pad ducks on every beat and swells back in between. Lengthen Release for a slower pump, or shorten it for a tight, subtle push.

The follower listens to a melody and its Trigger output fires a clap every time a note rises above the Threshold, so the drum part is written by the tune. Raise Threshold to skip the softer notes, or change Detector to RMS.

A slow Attack and long Release turn a sparse drum loop into a gentle level that fades a drone in and out, so the drone breathes with how busy the drums are. Shorten both times to make it follow each hit instead.

With Rectify set to None (signed), the follower becomes a slew limiter: stepped random values glide into one another and bend a voice's pitch. Raise Attack for slow climbs and Release for slow falls, or play with the Gain.

A full-range saw riff and a beat are squeezed through a steep Low Cut, a steep High Cut and a Bell boost in the midrange: the sound shrinks to a tiny speaker. Switch bands 1 and 6 off to open the sound again, or move the Bell around.
A narrow Bell boosted by 14 dB glides up and down the spectrum under an LFO on its Freq, so the riff sings like a wah pedal. Widen Q for a gentler vowel, or give the LFO a faster rate.

A mix of bass, riff and drums gets a Low Shelf lift, a small Bell cut in the muddy low mids and a High Shelf cut: a darker, rounder balance. Flip the Shelf gains to the other side for a bright, thin version.
Two Notch bands moved in opposite directions by one slow LFO carve gaps in a sustained saw line, giving a hollow, phaser-like sweep without any feedback. Raise Q for thinner, sharper gaps.
A High Cut with the steepest 48 dB/oct slope is pushed open by a slow LFO over a riff and beat, like a filter riser. Choose a gentler Slope for a softer glide, or turn the sweep depth down.

A held saw chord goes into the bank while a drum loop drives the Sidechain: with Vocode up, each band opens only when the drums have energy in that range, so the chord chatters in the rhythm of the beat. Change Vocode, Release or Q to tighten or smear it.

A bright, buzzy drone passes through only a few neighbouring bands; an LFO on Scan slides that window up and down the spectrum like a slow wah. Widen Width for a fuller sound, or raise Q for whistling.

Plain noise goes into ten very narrow bands tuned to a minor pentatonic scale (Tuning set to Scale), so it rings as a soft, wind-like chord. Change Root or Scale, move Shift to transpose the whole set, or lower Q to lose the pitch.

Odd bands go left and even bands go right, so one saw arpeggio is pulled apart into two interlocking halves. Swing Odd/Even with the LFO and the sound moves between the speakers; set Stereo to Normal to hear it fold back to the middle.

Jacks is set to Bands: four of the ten band outputs go to their own mixer channels, panned from left to right, so the low end of a drum-and-bass loop sits in the middle and brighter bands spread out. Change the mixer levels to rebalance the spectrum, or tilt the bank with Tilt.

A raw saw bass runs through a warm ladder-style low-pass whose Cutoff is opened by an envelope on every note, then closes again for a classic squelch. Raise Resonance or Drive for more bite, or switch Type to another ladder.
The Type is set to a four-stage phaser: a slow LFO sweeps Cutoff through a held, slightly detuned saw chord so the notches drift up and down. Try the 2-Pole phaser, more Resonance, or a faster LFO.

A whole drum loop goes through the unit-gain band-pass type while an LFO sweeps Cutoff: the beat shrinks to a thin radio sound, then opens up again. Move Mix to blend the original back in, or lower Resonance for a wider band.

The sequencer's pitch also goes into the filter, and Key Track at full makes Cutoff follow every note, so high and low notes keep the same brightness. Lower Key Track to hear the low notes go dull, or move Mode to morph from low-pass to high-pass.

Type is the flanger algorithm: a long single note rings through a sweeping comb of resonances that rise and fall with a slow LFO on Cutoff. Push Resonance for a metallic jet sound, or pull Mix back for a gentle swirl.

A flowing melody on the Formant Osc while a slow LFO sweeps the Formant peak, so the tone opens and closes like a voice changing vowels, without a filter anywhere. Move Formant by hand, or raise Narrow for a more nasal peak.

A decaying envelope sweeps the formant peak up and down on every note, giving a squelchy bass that behaves like a resonant filter although there is none. Change Narrow for a sharper squelch, or lengthen the decay for a longer wow.
Slow chord roots on the Formant Osc with Spread and Body opened up make a breathy, choir-like pad that sits wide in the stereo field. Turn Spread to zero for mono, or Roll up to soften the upper end.

A fast arpeggio while a Random module picks a new smooth Formant position every few beats: each note wears a different vowel. Raise Random's Smooth for glides between vowels, or Spread for bolder jumps.

With Tracking on Fixed, the formant peak stays put while the notes move, as in a real vowel across a sung tune, instead of rising with the pitch. Switch Tracking back to Ratio and the whole tone shifts with each note.

A saw pad is shifted up by a tiny Fine amount, and strong Feedback sends it round again, so the phasing sweep seems to climb forever. Make Fine negative and it falls forever; raise Mix to hear more of the swirl.

With Shift raised on the 200 Hz range and Mix at 100 %, the harmonics of a pad move by a fixed number of Hz instead of staying in tune, so it turns into clanging, inharmonic bells. Reduce Shift toward zero to bring the pad back to a normal pitch.
Spread sends the left channel up and the right channel down by the same few Hz, so a mono riff becomes wide and slowly beating without any delay. Close Spread to hear the plain mono sound again.

A broken beat is shifted down a few hundred Hz with some Feedback, so the kick loses its pitch and the snare and hats turn into clanking robot hits. Move Shift through zero and up to hear the effect change character.

The Shifter's own Sin output, a control signal that runs at the shift rate, opens and closes a filter on the same riff, so the phasing and the filter wobble stay locked together. Change Fine to speed up or slow down both.
With Cycle on, the Function is a free-running rise-and-fall LFO: its A output opens and closes the filter on a plucked line. Change Rise and Fall for a lopsided sweep, or Shape to bend the slopes.

Cycle is off, so every sequencer gate triggers one rise-and-fall: the A output shapes the volume and the B output, lagging behind through Spread, opens the filter slightly later. Try a slower Rise for swells or a longer Fall for ringing notes.

A, B, C and D are the same slow cycle at different delays, set by Spread, and here each one moves something else: filter cutoff, resonance, oscillator shape and reverb size. Raise Spread to pull them further apart, or lower it to make them move as one.

Locked to the beat with Sync, the Function acts as a rhythmic pump on a held pad: Fall sets how fast the volume swells back after each bounce. Change Sync for a faster or slower pulse, or Shape for a softer curve.

One trigger per bar starts a long swell that fades a pad in and out; when it finishes, its End output triggers a second Function that plays a short chime. Lengthen the first Fall to push the chimes later.

Coin-flip steps (?) and quiet ghost notes (o) make a drum pattern that breathes differently on every pass; Swing adds a lazy lean. Turn a track's Chance knob down for fewer hits, or set Dice to Fixed to lock one version in.
Steps marked 2 and 3 fire quick repeats inside one step: two on the snare, a rising run of three on the hats. Ratchet Decay fades each repeat out, so try raising it for a bouncing-ball feel.

Four tracks of different lengths (3, 4, 5 and 7 steps) each pluck one note of a chord, so the pattern only realigns after 420 steps and keeps shifting shape. Change a Length setting by one to get a different cycle.

Steps marked ! only play while the Fill input is high and steps marked - only while it is low, so a square LFO that holds Fill for the last bar of every four swaps the main beat for a busy fill. Some steps are nudged early or late for a human feel; Nudge Depth scales them all.

Slow square LFOs patched into the Mute inputs bring the four tracks in and out on their own cycles of 2, 4 and 8 bars, so a simple pattern arranges itself. Patch a different LFO Sync into a mute jack to rewrite the structure.

A recording of steady rain is played as a cloud of 300 ms grains, scattered wide by Spread and slowly scanned by an LFO on Position, with Blur smoothing the grains into a soft, deep curtain of sound. Lower Size and raise Density for a crisp downpour, or raise Pitch for a lighter, more distant shower.

In Triggered mode each sequencer step fires one short, percussive grain of rain, and the sequencer's Pitch is patched into Grains' Pitch input, so the raindrops play a tune. Texture at 100 % gives a plucked attack. Change Size for longer notes, Pitch Quant to Off for glides, or Pitch Jitter for a more scattered melody.

A single recorded piano note is turned into a slow, endless pad: grains of 600 ms drawn from around Position, detuned by Pitch Jitter and snapped by Pitch Quant to octaves and fifths, so the cloud sings in stacked octaves and fifths. A slow LFO moves Position from the attack to the tail. Try Size, Density and Feedback.

A struck gong is stretched into grains an octave higher, with Feedback and Blur feeding the cloud back into itself so each hit blooms into a glassy halo. A sequencer plays the gong's pitch (Pitch input) and fires a grain burst on each note. Raise Feedback for a longer afterglow, or lower Pitch to hear the gong's own size.

Triggered mode with Sync on 1/16: a grid of tiny, percussive grains cut from a crotale recording makes a glittering rhythmic stutter, with some grains reversed. A stepped random source jumps Position on every beat so each bar pulls a different piece of the bell. Raise Density for bursts, or Size for a ringing tail.

A minor progression (i, VI, III, VII) runs with the transport; its Tone outputs hold a warm pad, Bass walks underneath and a sequenced lead on the bus rewrites itself to stay inside each chord's scale. Change Key or Scale and the whole board follows.

With Advance set to Trigger, the progression moves one chord every time a trigger arrives; here an off-beat sequencer rhythm does the stepping and each change plucks the chord. Edit the trigger rhythm and the chords change when you decide.

A slow two-step sequence feeds the Transpose input, so after four bars the whole progression, bass and follower lead move up two semitones together. Change the transposing sequence to climb through more keys.

Four chosen chords written as fixed roots and rich qualities: minor 11, dominant 13, major 7 sharp 11 and dominant 7 sharp 9. The Tone outputs get the whole stack. Click a slot in the view to try another quality.

Manual source: one held fifth in E Phrygian Dominant, with a follower line that wanders by Variation but never leaves the scale. Change Degree or the scale to colour the drone, or Quality to a richer chord.

A pentatonic riff loops by itself; the Keyboard's Pitch output goes to the sequencer's Transpose input, so playing a key moves the whole riff to that note. Change Octave to shift the range of the keys, or Priority to choose which key wins when you hold several.

A soft bell arpeggio plays underneath; the Keyboard's Pitch and Gate drive a separate saw lead, and Glide is set to 0.25 s so notes slide into each other as you play. Raise Glide for slower portamento or bring it to 0 for clean steps.

A bass loop plays alone until you press keys: the Keyboard's Pitch, Trigger and Velocity strike a marimba-like Modal Voice, so harder Velocity makes brighter hits. Try the Velocity knob, or play a run down the keys.

The Keyboard's Notes output feeds an Arpeggiator set to Latch: a bass line and beat run alone until you press a few keys, and when you let go they keep arpeggiating until you press a new chord. Change the Arpeggiator's Pattern or Octaves to hear the same keys differently.

Hold is on and Priority is Lowest, so the keys you click stay down and the lowest one sets a slow drone under a gentle bell melody. Click the same key again to release it, or press All off to clear the keys.

A small band passes through a Level Meter on its way to the output: watch the RMS bars dance and the peak marks stop at the top of each hit, with the clip lights staying dark. Turn the band's mixer up until a clip light shows, then back off.

patches.name: Level Meter: Level Ducks the Pad

preset.description: The drums run through a Level Meter whose Level output, inverted, pulls the pad's volume down on every kick: a sidechain pump made from a meter. Raise Response for slower, wider pumping, or turn the cable amount down for a gentler duck.

panels.name: Level Meter: Level Ducks the Pad

controls.text: Level Meter: Level Ducks the Pad

patches.name: Level Meter: Loudness Opens the Filter

preset.description: The loudness of a drum loop, read by the Level Meter's Level output, opens the filter of a saw bass: loud passages sound bright, quiet ones muffled, like an envelope follower. Change Response for smoother or twitchier brightness.

panels.name: Level Meter: Loudness Opens the Filter

controls.text: Level Meter: Loudness Opens the Filter

preset.description: Two Level Meters sit either side of a Compressor: the first shows the raw band, the second what is left after the squeeze, so you can see the dynamics shrink. Drop the Compressor's Threshold and watch the second meter's peaks come down.

patches.name: Level Meter: Watching a Tail Fade

preset.description: Sparse bell notes ring into a long reverb, and a Level Meter with its Floor at minus 96 dB lets you watch the tail die away to nothing, long after the notes are gone. Change Floor to minus 24 dB to see how much of the tail the meter hides.

panels.name: Level Meter: Watching a Tail Fade

controls.text: Level Meter: Watching a Tail Fade

preset.description: One slow LFO gently bends the pitch of a held lead and a second one swells its volume; Fade lets the vibrato arrive only after the note has settled. Raise the vibrato Rate or the cable amounts, or move Fade to zero.

A triangle LFO locked to eighth notes sweeps the low-pass filter of a bass line, a classic wobble that stays in time with the drums. Change Sync for a slower or faster wobble, switch the output you cable from triangle to square, or raise Resonance.

The LFO's Random Step wave picks a new level every sixteenth and sends it to the filter, so a repeating line is coloured differently on each step, always the same way for a given Seed. Change Seed for another pattern or switch to Random Smooth.

Two LFOs, half a cycle apart through Phase, raise and lower the left and right volume of a pad in opposite directions, so it travels across the stereo field. Change Rate, or set both Phase values the same to hear it collapse to a plain tremolo.

A square LFO locked to sixteenths chops a held pad into a rhythmic gate, and its Cycle output also triggers the hi-hat on every pulse. Move Pulse Width to make the chops shorter or longer, or change Sync for another pattern.

A broken beat is driven 18 dB into a fast, low-ceiling Limiter: the peaks are shaved flat and the whole kit gets denser and louder at the same top level. Lower Input to hear the open dynamics return, or lower Ceiling for more squash.

A bass line and a four-on-the-floor beat are pushed hard into a Limiter with a long Release, so the bass dips on every kick and comes back slowly. Shorten Release for a tight, clean sound or lengthen it for a heavy breathing groove.
A pad that swells slowly in and out is driven into a low-ceiling Limiter, which holds it at one constant level: the fade-ins vanish and notes simply appear. Pull Input down to let the swells return.

A kick-heavy beat is limited, and the Limiter's Reduction output opens the cutoff of a filter on a lead, so the lead brightens exactly when the drums hit hardest. Raise Input for more reduction and a wider swing.

The finished mix of lead, bass and drums passes through a transparent Limiter with 5 ms Lookahead and a ceiling just under full scale, as the last module before the output. Raise Input and watch the reduction build while the peaks never pass the ceiling.

Four lines of 16, 5, 7 and 9 rows start together and slide against each other, so the bass, a lead, an arp and a stab only meet again after 5040 rows. The drift panel in the view shows each track's place. Change a track's Length or Speed to move the meeting point.

A bass line that uses the effect column: slide cells tie notes together with a glide and retrigger cells split a row into quick repeats. A second track answers with probability cells, so it never plays quite the same bar. Edit the Fx column in the view.

The same twelve-row length on four tracks, but at speeds of one, two thirds, three halves and three quarters: the tracks stay in a simple ratio and phase slowly against each other, like gears. Change one Speed and the whole weave shifts.

Three patterns of 16, 16 and 32 rows run in an order list: a verse, a verse with a new bass note, and a long answer. Tracks restart with each pattern here (Tracks: Per pattern), so every section begins together; switch it to Free-run and the drift carries on.

Tracks 1 to 3 each hold one voice of a chord at different lengths and speeds, and all three Notes outputs play one polyphonic Voice Cell: the harmony shifts as the three tracks drift. Track 4 adds a quiet high bell. Try the Quantize setting with another Scale.

Two gate patterns, one irregular and one straight eighths, feed the Logic module: where both hit (And) the kick plays, where only one does (Xor) the snare, and Or adds a soft hat on every hit of either. Change either lane on the Drum Grid and the drums rearrange themselves.

Each kick flips the flip-flop, so its output is high on one beat and low on the next; one arpeggio plays while it is high and a second one while it is low, taken from a chained Logic module that inverts it. Speed up the flips for a stutter, or reset them for a fixed phrase.

A square wave is fed into Logic, and its Rise output fires a kick when the wave goes up, Fall a snare when it comes down, and Change a closed hat at either edge. Narrow the square's pulse width and the snare moves away from the kick.

Three square waves at different speeds are combined three ways: Nor fires the kick when all of them are low, Nand the snare when any one drops, and Not-A a rim on the second half of A's cycle. Change any wave's speed to find new patterns.

Three sequencers of three, four and five steps run in parallel and drift in and out of phase; Logic turns their gates into a drum part, with And as a rare accent on the kick, Xor on the rim and Or on the hats. Change a sequencer's Length and the whole rhythm shifts.

A bright saw is silent until each sequencer trigger pings the gate: it snaps open and then darkens as it closes, like a plucked string. Raise Response for longer notes, Ping for harder hits, or switch Cell to Fast.

Low, sine-like tones pinged by the drum grid through the Fast cell sound like tuned skin drums, with a short, sharp attack and a quick roll-off. Try Resonance for a ringing pitch, or change Response to tighten or loosen the hits.

With the Slow memory cell and a slow LFO on the CV input, the gate opens and closes like breathing over a held two-voice chord, getting brighter as it swells. Change the LFO rate or the Response to alter the pace.

patches.name: Low Pass Gate: Filter Mode Bass

preset.description: Mode is set to LP, so the gate only acts as a filter on a steady buzzing bass: every ping opens the cutoff and it dulls again, while a Level of about a quarter keeps the note audible between hits. Switch Mode to VCA to hear only the volume change.

panels.name: Low Pass Gate: Filter Mode Bass

controls.text: Low Pass Gate: Filter Mode Bass

preset.description: A softly pinged triangle wave with some Bleed lets a little signal through even when the gate is shut, so each note sits on a quiet bed of sound. Raise Bleed to blur the gaps, or lower Brightness for a more muffled wooden tone.

The Pluck model struck by the sequencer's trigger: its built-in decay and low-pass gate shape every note, so no envelope or VCA is needed. Turn Decay for longer strings, Tone for brightness and Shape for how hard the string is hit.

The Vowel model holds slow notes while a slow LFO walks Tone through the vowels, so the choir seems to sing a different syllable on every phrase. Turn Blend to change the voice or Shape for brightness.

The FM model as a tine-and-bell keyboard sound: Tone sets the modulator ratio and an envelope on Shape gives each key a sparkle that fades. Change Tone to hop between ratios, or raise Blend for more of the second voice.

Three Macro Oscs on the Kick, Snare and Metal models are struck by a drum grid: a whole beat from one module type. Change each model's Decay and Tone to tune the kit, or switch a model for other percussion.
The Modal model struck by a trigger rings like a wooden bar. Tone moves from soft wood to bright metal, Decay lengthens the ring, and Accent from the velocity gives the loud and soft notes.

Four sources (bass, chords, lead, drums) go into a 4 by 2 matrix, each with its own left and right gain: the bass sits in the middle, the chords lean left, the lead right and the drums are spread. Click a crosspoint to change how much of a source goes to which side.

Two stored snapshots: A is a sparse scene with bass and a pad, B adds drums and the lead on the right. A slow LFO on Morph blends smoothly between them, so the arrangement builds and thins by itself. Drag Morph by hand, or edit a snapshot's crosspoints.

A saw arpeggio and a square arpeggio enter a 2 by 2 matrix. Each output carries a mix of both, and two LFOs in opposite phase move the crossing gains, so the voices drift from one side to the other and back. Change a gain to a negative value to hear phase effects.

One plucked line fans out to four outputs through four crosspoints with different gains; outputs 1 and 2 go to the speakers and outputs 3 and 4 pass through delays on the other side, so a single melody turns into a stereo echo field. Raise or lower the 1 to 3 and 1 to 4 gains to place the echoes.

Four loud parts are summed into one output with every crosspoint at full gain, and the Output Stage setting is Soft clip, so peaks are rounded off instead of cutting hard. Try Clean and Normalize for the other behaviours, or turn Level 1 down to rebalance.

A pentatonic phrase plays once every four bars; a beat after its last note the Mirror answers with the same notes played backwards, rhythm included. Change Length to turn more or fewer notes around, or Speed to play the reply slower.

The phrase is mirrored in pitch around its first note and pulled into A minor pentatonic, so the reply climbs where the original fell. Turn Axis to Mean or Fixed to move the mirror, and Transpose to lift the reply.
Answer mode: the module listens to the phrase, waits for the pause, plays the mirror image as a reply and listens again, ignoring itself while it answers. Try Reply Invert or Rotate, or a longer Gap.
A four-note motif comes back with its pitches rotated two places along the same rhythm, so it sounds related but different. Change Rotate, or Mode to Mirror, to turn it another way.

A slow LFO sweeps the Mode knob, so each reply is a different turn of the phrase: reversed, inverted, rotated or mirrored. Patch your own modulation into Mode, or set Start to Trigger to play replies by hand.

With no modulator patched, the internal oscillator multiplies a simple melody in analog ring mode, giving clangorous bell tones. Change Osc Tune to move between consonant and metallic, or sweep Algorithm to the neighbours.

In vocoder mode a buzzing saw carrier is shaped by the drum beat as modulator, so the pad seems to pump and speak in the rhythm of the kit. Change Timbre for a different band balance, or the saw's pitch for another vowel colour.

Bitwise mode combines a bass line with the internal oscillator number by number, producing digital edge and odd harmonics that move with Osc Tune. Switch Bitwise Op between XOR, AND and OR, or sweep Timbre.

A slow triangle LFO walks the Algorithm knob from crossfade through fold and ring modulation and back, so the same two tones keep changing character. Narrow the LFO's amount to stay in one family, or move Timbre by hand.

The last algorithm adds harmonics to a plain sine bass line, with a slow LFO moving Timbre from a pure tone to a bright, organ-like glow. Try Quality for cleaner top end, or Mix to blend the pure sine back in.

A mallet strikes a bar-shaped body on every step of a looping pentatonic pattern. Geometry sits at 50 % (a bar), Damping and Strike Timbre keep it woody. Try Geometry towards 0 for a string, towards 100 % for a bell, or Position at 50 % to cancel the even partials.

No mallet at all: a Bow sings a bell-shaped body for as long as each gate is held. Contour at a low value gives a slow swell and long release, so the chords of the sequence bloom into each other. Lower Bow Timbre for a light, airy bow, or raise Damping to hear the bell become wood.

A string-like body (Geometry 0 %) is excited only by Blow with a high Blow Timbre: above 60 % the breath couples with the body like an air jet and it sings on its own, with a little breath noise on top. Move Blow Timbre across 60 % to hear the voice appear, or add Strike for a tongued start.

Audio from a drum beat goes into Ext In with every built-in exciter at 0, so the module is a resonator in a room: the drums ring a tuned plate. Change Coarse to retune the plate, Geometry to move from string to plate to bell, Damping for how long it keeps ringing.

A hard, bright strike on a stiff string (Geometry 25 %) is a plucked-string sound, played as a broken chord in an open room. Position sets where the string is plucked and Strike Timbre how hard the pick is. Lengthen Damping for a harp, or shorten it for a muted pluck.

The sequencer's notes pass through a Monitor on their way to a synth voice: its table lists each note on and off with pitch and velocity as it happens. Change a step's note or velocity in the sequencer and read the difference in the table.

A slow LFO runs through the Monitor's CV input before it sweeps the filter of a gentle line: the readout shows the value moving between its extremes while you hear the same thing. Change the LFO's rate or wave and watch the shape change.

patches.name: Monitor: Gate Meter on the Kick

preset.description: The kick's gate from the Drum Grid goes through the Monitor's gate meter, which lights on every hit and shows how long the gate lasts, before it triggers the drum. Lengthen the Drum Grid's Gate Length and watch the meter stay lit.

panels.name: Monitor: Gate Meter on the Kick

controls.text: Monitor: Gate Meter on the Kick

preset.description: A ping-pong delay bounces a pluck line left and right through the Monitor's audio meters, so you see the two channels take turns. Raise the Floor to see only the loud part, or lower Response to make the bars fall slowly.

One Monitor watches four kinds of signal on a single synth voice: the notes going in, a vibrato CV, the envelope's gate and the stereo audio coming out. Change the vibrato LFO or the sequence and see which panel reacts.

Two sine oscillators multiplied together make only their sum and difference tones, which are not whole-number multiples of the note: clangorous bells that fade with each strike. Change the second oscillator's Coarse to retune the bell.

A saw melody goes into X1 and a sine LFO into Y1, with Bias Y1 lifting the LFO above zero so it works as a smooth tremolo; without the bias the sound would also flip its phase. Lower Bias Y1 toward zero for a deeper, rougher ring.

Every note's decay envelope is multiplied by a slow LFO before it reaches the filter, so the notes open the filter wide when the LFO is high, hardly at all when it is low and even invert when it dips below zero. Raise Bias Y1 to keep the LFO positive.

Both multipliers ring-modulate the same saw melody, one with a modulator at a fifth above and one at a ratio that sits between notes, and each goes to its own side: left is nearly musical, right is metallic. Change either modulator's Coarse to move the clangour.

A whole drum loop is multiplied by a low sine so each hit turns pitched and robotic, mixed with the untouched loop underneath. Raise Oversampling to keep the highs clean, or change the sine's Coarse to tune the robot.

Two neurons charge up, fire and listen to each other, and that conversation is a drum pattern: A fires the kick, B the snare, and the logic outputs add hats and claps where they agree or differ. Change the Threshold or Leak of either neuron and the rhythm re-forms.

Neuron A's gate plays the notes and its membrane level, passed through a Quantizer, picks the pitch: as the neuron charges the notes climb, then drop when it fires. Lower the Threshold for a faster tune, or raise Leak to flatten the climb.

With Cross on Gate, each neuron's firing nudges the other, so a low bass note from A is answered by a high bell from B. Set Cross to Off and the two stop listening and drift apart; change B's W3 to turn the answer into a hesitation.

The neurons' membrane levels (A Out and B Out) are slow, irregular swells here: one fades a pad in and out and the other opens its filter. Lower Leak for longer swells, or raise Sharp on a neuron for a harder snap at the top.

A slow triangle LFO feeds the neurons' inputs: when it is high they fire fast and when it is low they go quiet, so a bass, tom and hat pattern speeds up and thins out in waves. Change the LFO Rate or the neuron weights to change the ebb and flow.

Blue noise, cut short by an envelope and high-passed, is played as hi-hats from a drum grid pattern over a soft kick. Slide Colour toward white for a duller tick, or toward blue for a thinner, brighter sizzle.
Brown noise swells and recedes as two slow LFOs open a low-pass filter and the level together, like waves washing in. Raise Colour for foam and hiss, or speed up the LFO for a stormier sea.
White noise through a very resonant band-pass filter that follows the sequencer's pitch: a breathy, whistling tune with no oscillator at all. Lower Resonance for a wind that only hints at pitch.

Every four bars a ramp sweeps Colour from dark brown to bright violet while a filter opens, building tension over a steady beat before it drops back. Change the LFO's Sync to lengthen or shorten the build.

The white, pink, brown and blue outputs go to four mixer channels whose pans drift on slow LFOs, then through a gently resonant filter into a hall. Mute channels on the mixer to hear each colour alone.
A two-bar bass line, recorded earlier, loops over a beat. Set Mode to Overdub and play along to add notes on top, press Undo to take the last layer off again, or Clear to start over.

A one-bar sixteenth-note figure is played with 55 % Probability, so every pass keeps a different set of its notes. Change Seed for another sequence of passes, or raise Probability to 100 % for the full figure.
A two-bar tune loops at half speed, so it takes four bars to come round and every note is twice as long. Set Speed to Double or Normal to hear the same notes at other speeds.

A loosely played one-bar riff, quantized to sixteenths by a Strength that a slow LFO sweeps from none to full: you hear the take tighten and loosen again. Turn Strength up for a fixed amount, or try Quantize 1/8T.

A sparse two-bar loop feeds a Note Echo that climbs the scale and fans into chord tones, so a handful of recorded notes becomes a shimmering figure. Mute the Echo's Original or change its Rate to reshape it.

A sequencer's notes come in, and Notes to CV hands out pitch, gate, trigger and velocity: the velocity opens the envelope harder on the accented steps. Try Retrigger Off to hear the tied notes run together.
Tied notes slide into each other because Glide is up and Glide Mode is Legato Only; separate notes still jump. Turn Glide to 0 for a plain bass, or set Glide Mode to Always to slide into every note.

patches.name: Notes to CV: Lowest and Highest

preset.description: A Chord Quantizer sends four-note chords as notes; one Notes to CV follows the lowest note for a bass, another the highest for a bright lead. Change either Priority to Last or First to follow a different note of the chord.

panels.name: Notes to CV: Lowest and Highest

controls.text: Notes to CV: Lowest and Highest

preset.description: Overlapping long notes with Retrigger Off and a slow Glide make the pad drift from chord root to chord root without restarting its envelope. Switch Retrigger to On and every note swells again.

patches.name: Notes to CV: Trigger Out Kick

preset.description: Every note that arrives also leaves Notes to CV as a trigger, here firing a kick drum in step with a bass line, while Pitch plays the bass. Change the sequencer's pattern and the kick follows it.

panels.name: Notes to CV: Trigger Out Kick

controls.text: Notes to CV: Trigger Out Kick

preset.description: Eight slow, related movements are spread over a pad: the filter, the oscillator shape and the reverb size each follow a different one, so the sound breathes without ever repeating exactly. Change Rate, Spread and Drift on the module to speed up or loosen the group.

Six of the eight outputs swell six notes of a chord in and out, so the harmony rearranges itself in a slow, natural way. Lower Scatter to make the voices move more alike, or turn Spread negative to reverse the order.

At a faster Rate with plenty of Drift, the same eight movements become a restless wobble: they open the filter, change the tone and add resonance to a plucked line, never twice the same way. Slow Rate and Drift down for a calmer feel.

With Lock set to Bars the group repeats in step with the song, so the filter movement over a bass line and beat comes back exactly each time. Switch Lock back to Free and the same movement slips out of time.
Four held notes each wander across the stereo field, steered by different outputs, while Twist bends how the group is related. Change Twist and Spread to change how the voices follow each other.

A bass line on one Oscillator while a slow LFO turns Shape from triangle through saw toward square, so the same note keeps changing colour. Set Shape by hand to freeze a waveform, or move Pulse Width for a thinner square.

A lead oscillator is reset by the sequencer's gate on every note, while a slow LFO pushes its Coarse tuning upward: the classic tearing sync sweep. Turn Shape toward the saw for more bite, or lower the LFO amount for a calmer tone.

A second Oscillator frequency-modulates the first through its FM input, and a decaying envelope on FM Depth makes each bell strike bright and then mellow. Change the modulator's Coarse for different bell families, or raise FM Depth for glassier tones.

The main output and the Sub output (one octave down) are mixed under a drum loop, with Pulse Width moving slowly for a hollow, breathing bass. Mute the Sub channel on the mixer to hear how much weight it adds.

Three Oscillators a few cents apart play slow chord roots, one pushed a fifth up, and a reverb spreads them wide. Change Fine on any oscillator for faster beating, or Shape for a brighter or softer pad.

A whole kit from three Perc Voices in different engines: a Modal kick (Tone 8 %, Sweep high), a Noise Bank snare with a wide Morph and a membrane-toned Modal tom. Velocity from the grid goes into Accent, so soft hits are duller as well as quieter. Try Tone and Decay on each voice, or Drive on the kick.

In the FM engine the partials modulate one sine carrier, so Morph is the modulation index: bright on the attack, purer in the tail. A sequencer's Pitch tunes the hits, which makes a melody of toms. Raise Morph for metal, lower Decay for wood blocks, or switch Track on to let the pitch follow during the ring.

The Modal engine with Tone at 85 % and Morph high lets the upper partials of a metallic set ring out like struck glass, with long Decay and low Damp. A slow sequence hits the bell, and a second, lower bell answers on the off-beat. Change Seed to get a different bell, or Tone to walk from bell to bar to drum.

Noise Bank at Tone 100 % is metal: a short one is a closed hat, a long one an open hat, and the closed hat's trigger is patched into the open hat's Choke so it cuts the ring off. A third voice with a very long Decay is a gong that swells in once per phrase. Try Damp, Morph and Pitch on the hats.

Noise Bank with a narrow Morph rings its band-pass filters almost pitched, the sound of a steel drum or a tuned block. A sequencer plays the pitch and each hit gets a small Spread of stereo width. Raise Morph towards 100 % for a noisier shaker, or change Damp to shorten the shimmer.
A saw riff passes a four-stage Phaser at a slow Rate with moderate Feedback: two soft notches slide up and down the sound. Change Stages for a busier or gentler sweep.
Twelve stages and strong negative Feedback on a held pad carve many narrow notches that sweep through the sound with a hollow, vocal quality. Try positive Feedback for a brighter, ringing sweep.

With Spread at maximum the left and right LFOs are far apart, so the notches move in opposite places in each ear and a mono pluck melody floats around the stereo field. Lower Spread to centre the movement.
A fast Rate with shallow Depth and few Stages gives a quick, rotary-like shimmer on a held organ-style tone. Slow Rate down for a classic sweep or deepen Depth to add warble.

Pink noise through a ten-stage Phaser with high Feedback turns into a rolling, whooshing jet over a quiet beat. Change Centre to move the sweep higher or lower, or reduce Feedback for a softer whoosh.

patches.name: Pitch Follower: Voice to Synth Bridge

preset.description: A bright plucked melody is followed note by note, and two soft synth voices play it for you an octave and a fifth lower, each note opened by the follower's Gate. Try Smooth Glide-like values on Glide to slide between the notes, or raise Confidence to hear the bridge hesitate.

panels.name: Pitch Follower: Voice to Synth Bridge

controls.text: Pitch Follower: Voice to Synth Bridge

preset.description: A melody that leaps across two octaves is followed, and its Pitch opens the filter on a held two-note drone: low notes make the drone dark, high notes make it shine. Change the filter's Keytrack to make the effect stronger or gentler.

patches.name: Pitch Follower: Only Clear Tones Pass

preset.description: A source alternates every bar between a clear melody and bursts of noise. The follower's Confidence drops for the noise, so the chime voice it drives plays the tune and falls silent in between. Lower the Confidence knob to let the noise start false notes.

panels.name: Pitch Follower: Only Clear Tones Pass

controls.text: Pitch Follower: Only Clear Tones Pass

preset.description: A jumpy melody on a sound with a loud second harmonic is the hard case for any pitch tracker. Octave Guard Firm and a Vote of 5 keep the follower on the right note, and a Quantizer tidies it onto the scale for a plucked voice. Set Guard to Off and Vote to Off and listen for octave slips.

A slow, legato melody is followed with a long Glide, so the synth slides from note to note like a portamento voice. The Env output opens a filter and the delay mix with each note's loudness. Shorten Glide for steps, or lengthen Env Release for a longer tail.

A pluck melody goes up an octave into a Pitch Shifter with Feedback and then a big reverb: each tail climbs in octaves into a glassy shimmer. Lower Feedback for a single octave halo or try +7 for a fifth.
A bass riff is blended with a copy an octave lower, doubling its depth at half Mix. Try -5 or -7 for a thick parallel line or raise Window for smoother, less grainy low notes.
The Shifter adds a line a fifth above the melody at half Mix, so every note is paired with a power-chord partner. Change Pitch to +4 for a major third, +3 for a minor third or -5 for a fourth below.

With Pitch at zero and just 12 cents of Fine plus a little Drift, a held pad is doubled by a slightly out-of-tune, wavering copy, which thickens it like an ensemble. Increase Drift for tape-like flutter or Fine for a wider detune.

Sparse notes enter a Pitch Shifter set a few semitones up with high Feedback: each echo is shifted again and spirals upward until it fades. Make Pitch negative and the spiral falls instead; add Drift for flutter.

A wobbly saw line with notes that do not belong to the key goes into a Pitch Snap set to hard correction in A minor pentatonic: every note jumps onto the scale with the stepped, robotic sound of a hard retune. Set Amount to 0 to hear the raw out-of-tune line, then bring it back up, or lower Speed for a softer glide.

patches.name: Pitch Snap: Drift Keeps the Vibrato

preset.description: A slow line with a 5.5 Hz vibrato and a drunken detune is pulled onto C major by a Pitch Snap with Drift at 100 %, so the average pitch is corrected while the vibrato stays alive.
