Set Drift to 0 and the vibrato is flattened into a steady tone; try a lower Drift Time for a quicker grip.

panels.name: Pitch Snap: Drift Keeps the Vibrato

controls.text: Pitch Snap: Drift Keeps the Vibrato

preset.description: One sloppy lead feeds three Pitch Snaps in parallel: the lead itself, one a fifth above (+7 Offset) and one an octave below (-12), each tuned to C major pentatonic and panned apart. Change an Offset to +4 for a major third or +12 for a bright octave double.

A Harmony Master runs an i-VI-III-VII progression on Bus A; a drunken lead is snapped to the chord tones and the Target output drives a bass oscillator, so the bass always plays the exact note the lead is corrected to. Change the Target setting to Chord + Scale to let passing notes through, or the Harmony Master's key to move everything.

patches.name: Pitch Snap: Stepped Offset with Formant

preset.description: A formant oscillator sings a steady line while a slow sequencer feeds the Offset jack, transposing the corrected voice in steps of 0, +5, +7 and +3 semitones with its vowel kept in place by Formant Preserve. Switch Formant off and the vowel slides with the pitch like a plain pitch shifter.

panels.name: Pitch Snap: Stepped Offset with Formant

controls.text: Pitch Snap: Stepped Offset with Formant

preset.description: The trigger track is five steps long and the note track seven, so each rhythm cycle meets a different pitch and the tune only repeats after thirty-five steps. Change the length of either track in the view to find another cycle.

A bass line built on a seven-step trigger track plays against a half-time beat, so the groove keeps leaning forward and landing again. The Track Ends output rings a hat whenever a track wraps around; try dragging Swing or Gate Scale.

The probability track gives each step a chance of sounding, so a Dorian marimba tune keeps thinning out and filling in. Push Prob. Bias up for a dense, almost fixed tune or down towards silence; change Seed to grow a different garden.

Some steps of the ratchet track split into two, three or four quick repeats, so a simple lead line stutters and rolls at odd places. Ratchet Amt scales how far the repeats go: bring it to 0 for a plain line, or leave it up for rolls.

Two stored patterns, a calm one and a busy one, share a voice, and a slow ramp on the Pattern input moves from one to the other at the next bar. Click a slot in the view to play it alone, or change Pattern Change to switch immediately.

A Pulse Generator synced to 1/8 is the clock of the melody, and its Jitter nudges every pulse a little early or late, so the tune sways like a human player. Turn Jitter to 0 for a rigid machine, or up to 40 % for a drunk one; the same Seed always gives the same wobble.

A whole kit from triggered pulses: the Ring output of each Pulse Generator is a pitched thump, tick or rattle. The tom fires a Burst of four pulses, a quick roll. Change Ring Freq for the tuning, Damping for how long they ring, Width for the colour.

One very short pulse per note makes the Ring resonance ping, and the sequencer's pitch tunes Ring Freq (1 V per octave), so each step is a glassy chime. A second, wider pulse a fifth above adds a darker partner. Try Damping for the length of the ring and Width for the brightness.

In External Width mode the Pulse Generator is a gate delay: each note's gate comes out 190 ms later, as long as it went in, and plays a second voice a fifth higher. The result is a hand-made echo of the melody. Change Delay for the spacing, or Rise and Fall to soften the echoed notes.

At audio rate the Pulse Generator is an oscillator: three of them at 110, 165 and 220 Hz, with slow LFOs on Width for a swaying pulse-width sound and soft Rise and Fall on the edges. Switch Double on for a hollow, comb-like voice, or change the Period to retune a note.
A hand clap on two and four over a steady kick and hats. Bursts sets how many hands you hear, Spread how loosely they land, and Tone how bright they sound.
Six slow, widely spread bursts with a long Decay sound like a crowd clapping together in a hall. Narrow Spread and lower Bursts to bring it back to a single pair of hands.
With Bursts at 1 and a short Decay the clap becomes a tight snap, played as a busy sixteenth pattern like a percussion loop. Raise Bursts one at a time to hear the snap turn back into a clap.
A low-toned clap with a long tail plays slow, spacious beats under a soft melody. Raise Tone to open it up, or shorten Decay to get a dry thump.
Three claps at different tones and Bursts roll over each other in an off-beat pattern, like a small audience losing the beat. Change Tone on each to separate the voices, or Spread to blur them.
A crash lands on the first beat of every two bars over a straight rock groove. Decay sets how long the wash lasts, Tone how bright it is, and Crunch how gritty.
The cymbal set to Ride plays a swung pattern over a light kick and brushed snare, jazz-style. Shorten Decay for a tighter ping, raise Tone for more bell.
A crash with a very long Decay and a darker Tone is sent into a huge reverb, so a few hits stack up into a slowly breathing wash. Raise Tone or shorten Decay to hear it become a normal crash.
A fast punk beat with a bright, crunchy crash splashing on every other beat. Turn Crunch down to polish it, or Tune up for a smaller splash.
A crash and a ride, each its own Cymbal, share a groove: the ride keeps time on the offbeats while the crash marks the phrase. Change Voice on either to swap the roles.
Closed hats shuffle along with swing while an open hat lifts every few beats and cuts the closed ones short. Lengthen Open Decay to hear it ring, or try Closed Decay for a looser, longer tick.
A long open hat rings on the offbeats and gets cut by the closed hat that follows, the way a real hat pedal behaves. Raise Open Decay for a longer wash, and notice the closed hit always shuts it off.
Hats with Tone and Crunch low and Tune pulled down sound muted and old, ticking quietly behind a lazy kick and snare. Raise Tone and Crunch to polish them up.
Fast sixteenth hats with Tone and Crunch at maximum sizzle over a driving kick. Lower Crunch for a cleaner shimmer, or turn Tune down if it feels too sharp.
Two hat voices tuned apart sit left and right and interlock into one busy pattern, one slightly darker and one brighter. Change the Tune on each to widen the gap.

patches.name: Punch Kick: Four on the Floor

preset.description: A steady kick on every beat with an offbeat open hat and a clap on two and four. Turn Decay down for a tight club thump or up for a boomy tail, and pull Sweep to hear the pitch drop in and out.

panels.name: Punch Kick: Four on the Floor

controls.text: Punch Kick: Four on the Floor

preset.description: A slow half-time groove over a very low kick with a long Decay and a gentle Sweep, so each hit rolls like a sub-bass note. Raise Tune to turn the boom into a thump, shorten Decay to hear it tighten.
Two kicks side by side, a low long one and a higher short one, trade phrases like a bass drum and its echo. Change Tune on either to re-pitch the pattern as a little melody.

A hard, driven kick with a strong click, and its tail sent into a dark reverb so every hit leaves a low rumble behind it. Push Drive and Attack for more bite, or lower Decay to make the rumble do the work.
A rounded, dull kick with almost no click or Drive sits under a soft plucked melody and quiet hats. Turn Attack and Drive up and the same pattern turns from lo-fi to punchy.
A hard, bright rim crack answers a soft kick in a syncopated pattern. Tune moves the crack up or down in pitch, and Decay lets it ring out or stops it dead.
Three rims tuned a fifth apart climb up and down like a small percussion ladder. Change Tune on any rim to bend the intervals, or lengthen Decay to let them overlap.
A low-tuned rim with the longest Decay rings through a roomy reverb in a sparse pattern, like a woodblock in a church. Raise Tune for a sharper tick.
The rim plays a five-hit clave over a gentle kick and hats, with a mellow bass line moving underneath. Raise Tune for a woodier tick, shorten Decay for dry crispness.
A sparse rim pattern bounces left and right through a tempo-synced delay, so a few hits fill the whole bar. Change the rim's Tune and Decay, and watch how the echoes follow.
A plain rock backbeat: the snare cracks on two and four over kick and hats. Raise Snappy for more rattle, lower it for a woodier hit, and turn Tone to move the body from hollow to bright.
A low, loose snare with a long Decay and lots of Snappy, thrown into a medium room so it blooms after each hit. Raise Tune to tighten it up, or cut Decay to dry it out.
A funky groove where soft ghost notes between the loud accents make the snare chatter. Velocity from the grid shapes each hit; try a short Decay and high Tune for a drier, tighter chatter.
Over a four-on-the-floor kick the snare tightens from a few hits into a full sixteenth roll and then stops. Short Decay keeps the roll clean; raise Snappy and Tone for a brighter build.
Two snares with Snappy at zero play a woody, tuned pair of drum heads under a warm bass line. Raise Snappy on either one and the wires come back; Tune moves the pair like a rototom.
Three toms tuned low, middle and high chase each other around a steady kick. Tune each tom to change the melody of the pattern, Bend to set how far the pitch falls on every hit.
High toms with the Bend turned all the way up zap downward like laser drops over a bouncy kick and snare. Pull Bend back to hear them settle into real toms.
A very low floor tom with a long Decay booms through a big room in a slow, ceremonial pattern. Raise Tune to bring it toward a conga, add Noise for a rougher skin.
Four toms with little Bend and no Noise are tuned to notes of a minor pentatonic scale, so the groove turns into a tuned melody. Change Tune on any tom to re-write the tune.
A fast fill of toms with plenty of Noise sounds like stretched, rattly skins, dropping a quick pitch on each hit. Lower Noise to clean them up, or raise Decay to let them ring over the kick.

In Quadrature mode the four LFOs are a quarter-turn apart, so four notes of a chord swell one after another in a rotating pattern. Change Rate to turn it faster, or switch Mode to Free to let each LFO run at its own speed.

Locked to the tempo in Divide mode, the four LFOs run at whole fractions of one rate: the fastest shapes the tone, slower ones open the filter over two, four and eight times as long. Change a Divide setting or switch Sync off to unlock it.

Phase mode keeps all four LFOs at the same rate but staggered by Spread. Here two of them sweep a separate filter for each channel, so the pad's brightness moves from left to right. Widen or narrow Spread, or change Rate 1 for a faster sweep.

In Free mode the four LFOs run at unrelated rates with different waves (sine, smooth random, triangle and stepped random); their Sum output moves the filter while the others change tone and resonance, an endlessly shifting texture. Change a Rate or Wave to steer it.

The LFOs follow a clock from the sequencer rather than a free rate, and a second, sparser gate patched to Hold freezes them for a moment. The result is a filter movement that stops and resumes in time with the notes. Change Clock Ratio for a faster or slower cycle.

A random line goes into channel A, where the note mask keeps only the notes of a C major seventh chord (C, E, G, B): any value lands on a chord tone, so the melody always outlines the harmony. Click other keys in the view's keyboard to change which notes are allowed.

One melody goes in on A; channels B, C and D transpose it in the scale by 4, 7 and minus 7 steps, which is a fifth up, an octave up and an octave down. Four voices play the thickened line. Change a Steps knob for other intervals.

Channel A turns each slow root into a ninth chord and plays it converging towards the middle over two octaves; B plays a sus2 chord downwards on the same clock. Change an Order or Chord and the run reshapes at once.

In Follow mode every channel listens to a Harmony Master on the bus: A snaps a random line to the current chord, B to chord and scale, C holds the chord root. When the progression moves, all three move with it. Change a Target, or the Harmony Master's key.

patches.name: Quantizer Suite: Track and Hold Slides

preset.description: Channel A follows a slow LFO but only changes pitch when its clock ticks, and Slew slides the voice between the held notes; channel B tracks continuously, so it keeps wobbling into new notes. Try Sample Trigger for hard steps, or Slew A at zero.

panels.name: Quantizer Suite: Track and Hold Slides

controls.text: Quantizer Suite: Track and Hold Slides

preset.description: A slow triangle LFO is a smooth, continuous voltage; the Quantizer turns it into stairs of pentatonic notes and fires a trigger on every new one, so the voice climbs and falls by itself. Widen Range for more octaves, or pick another Scale.

A stepped Random sends any value it likes; the Quantizer is clocked by a sequencer and, on each tick, snaps it into D Dorian, so the wandering always sounds like a tune. Try a different Scale (Whole Tone, Blues) or a smaller Range.

The sequencer plays an ordinary chromatic run, every semitone, and the Quantizer squeezes it into the five-note Hirajoshi scale, so repeated notes appear where the notes were pushed together. Switch Scale to Chromatic for the original run, or Rounding to Up.

A sine LFO sweeps a legato voice; the Quantizer picks scale notes but Glide turns each jump into a slide, like a fretless line stepping through a scale. Set Glide to zero for hard steps, or Rounding to Down to favour the lower note.

One sequencer line is quantized to the blues scale; a square LFO adds a step to the Transpose input every other bar, lifting the whole line to a new key area that is still in the scale. Change the LFO Sync or the amount of the Transpose cable.

Every eighth note the Random module picks a new value; with Semitones on they land on exact notes, so a steady rhythm plays a never-repeating tune. Raise Spread for a wider range, move Bias up or down to place it higher or lower, or change Seed for a new tune.

Loop at its top setting repeats an eight-step random pattern exactly, here moving a bass line's filter in time with the drums. Turn Loop down and the pattern slowly mutates, down to fully new values every step; change Length to repeat after more or fewer steps.

With Smooth turned up the random steps glide into one another, making a slow, irregular drift that moves a pad's brightness and tone. Lower Smooth to bring back the steps, or raise Rate to make the drift busier.

The Random module's trigger output fires a tom at irregular moments while its stepped output retunes it each time, a loose, tuned roll over a steady kick. Raise Rate for a busier roll or pull Spread in for a narrower range of pitches.

A high Bias and a narrow Spread keep the random notes in a bright upper range, like a music box wandering over a held drone. Set Bias to zero and widen Spread to bring the bells down across the whole range.

Every clock step Recall flips a coin for two gates: T1 plays the kick, T2 the snare, and the Clock output drives steady hats. T Bias leans the coin towards or away from firing, T Jitter adds extra randomness; try raising T Recall to repeat the recent past.

T Mode Ratchet turns the random gates into bursts of quick repeats, and each burst plays a bass note chosen by X from F Phrygian dominant. Lower X Spread for a narrower line, or move X Bias to put the bass higher or lower.

A slow sawtooth LFO raises both Recall knobs from 0 to 100 % over 16 bars: the melody starts out new on every step, gradually repeats itself more and more, and ends up as a locked loop before the cycle begins again. Move T Recall or X Recall yourself to freeze or free it at any time.

X Mode Sorted puts the three random voltages in ascending order, so X1, X2 and X3 always form a stack from low to high, and three voices play them as a changing chord. Switch X Mode to Independent and the voices cross over; change Scale for a different colour.

Sync is set to Free at 1.6 Hz, so Recall ticks on its own clock rather than the song's, and each random T1 gate rings a bell whose pitch is read from X on its own X clock. Change Rate to speed the shimmer up or slow it down.
A sequencer strums the Modal model with its own internal exciter and pitches it, so each note rings like a struck bell or bar. Move Structure to change the metal, and Damping to shorten the ring.

A plucked melody is fed into sympathetic strings tuned to a fixed root, so the drone strings glow along with whatever notes match them. Change Frequency to retune the drone, or Damping for a shorter shimmer.

The String model plays a bouncy bass-and-treble pattern, four voices deep so older notes keep ringing under new ones. Try Position for a hollower or brighter pluck, and Brightness for nylon versus steel.
A drum beat excites a Modal resonator that is tuned low, so every kick and hat rings the same plate-like body. Turn Dry up to bring the raw drums back, or sweep Frequency to retune the whole kit.

A slow LFO sweeps Structure through string, bar and plate territory while the same strummed notes play, so the instrument seems to change material as it rings. Patch the LFO into Brightness too, or change its speed.
Sparse, soft notes sink into a huge hall: Size is almost full, Decay is over twenty seconds and Pre-delay leaves each note clean before the bloom. Try Decay and Size together, or push Mix to 100 %.
A drum beat in a tiny, dry room: low Size, a short Decay and high Damping glue the kit together. Raise Size and Decay to move the same beat into a hall, or widen it with Width.

A square LFO closes the Freeze gate for a couple of bars at a time, holding whatever is in the tank as an endless chord, then lets go so the next phrase can be caught. Edit the LFO's Sync, or latch Freeze yourself.
Slow LFOs ride Size and Tone while Mod Depth swirls the tail, so the room seems to inhale and exhale around a gentle arpeggio. Every Verb knob modulates click-free: patch your own LFO into Decay.
A low plucked bass line in a cellar: Bass is boosted, Tone and Damping pull the tail dark, and Eco quality keeps it light. Lower Bass or lift Tone to hear the same room turn into a bright stairwell.

The Even family spreads hits as evenly as it can: four related rhythms of different density drive a kick, snare, hats and a rim. Turn Pattern to change all four grooves at once, or turn Width for longer or shorter gates.

Length 15 and the Prime family give four rhythms with uneven, prime-based spacing, each playing a different pluck of an A minor chord. Because the lengths never line up the same way twice, the figure keeps turning; try Family = Poly for a different split.

A stepped random LFO picks a new Pattern number every bar, and Change is set to Cycle so each new rhythm waits for the end of the current one: the part develops by itself without a break. Set Change to Step to switch mid-pattern, or turn the LFO cable down to stay near one groove.

With Complement set to Pairs, output 2 fills the gaps left by output 1 (and 4 those of 3), so a low and a high voice share one steady line like two hands. Switch Complement to Off to hear the raw rhythms collide, or to Avoid to keep them from landing together.

Length is Open, so the rhythms never loop, and the Seeded family makes up a fresh but related set from the Pattern number. Rotate nudges each rhythm against the others and Grid Free lets hits sit between steps; set Length back to 16 to hear a plain loop.
The default clap on two and four over a steady kick and hat. Raise Bursts for a bigger group, or Spread for looser, more human timing.
One burst with very small Spread turns the clap into a short, dry snap that sits on the offbeats. Raise Bursts one at a time to hear it turn back into a clap.
Many bursts spread wide, a long Decay and a big room make a small crowd clapping along. Lower Bursts and Spread to shrink the crowd back to one pair of hands.

patches.name: Ring Clap: Bright To Dark Clap

preset.description: A slow LFO sweeps the clap's Tone from dark to bright and back while a steady beat plays underneath. Turn Tone yourself to pick the colour you like.

panels.name: Ring Clap: Bright To Dark Clap

controls.text: Ring Clap: Bright To Dark Clap

preset.description: A rolling sixteenth-note clap feeds a tempo-synced delay for a swirling, rhythmic texture. Change Bursts and Decay to alter how dense each hit is.
A steady eighth-note cowbell on top of a four-on-the-floor kick and an open hat. Tone opens and closes the bell, Decay changes how much it rings.
A high and a low cowbell play an interlocking Latin pattern. The Tune of each bell sets the interval between them.
Low Tune, low Tone and a long Decay turn the cowbell into a muted, tolling bell. Raise Tone for a brighter strike.
Tone near the top and a short Decay give a sparkling pinged pulse over a driving kick. An LFO opens and closes Tone slowly.

patches.name: Ring Cowbell: Bell And Clap Shuffle

preset.description: A shuffled kit with a cowbell on the triplet-feel offbeats and a clap on two and four. Change the cowbell's Decay to move from dry tick to long clang.

panels.name: Ring Cowbell: Bell And Clap Shuffle

controls.text: Ring Cowbell: Bell And Clap Shuffle

preset.description: A crash on the first beat of every second bar carries the groove forward. Decay sets how long it rings; Tone moves the brightness.
Short Decay and a higher Tone give a ride-like ping in a swinging pattern. Stretch Decay for a washy ride, shorten it for a stick-on-metal feel.
A very long Decay and a huge reverb let a single cymbal bloom into an ambient wash. Shorten Decay or the reverb to hear its hit.
Tune and Tone low give a gong-like clang with a slow shimmer. Raise either to move toward a bright crash.
A steady dance beat with a cymbal on the off-beat whose Decay breathes in and out with an LFO. Open it up for a washy build, close it for tight tics.

patches.name: Ring Hats: Open And Closed Groove

preset.description: Closed hats on eighths with an open hat on the off-beat, which the next closed hat cuts off. Lengthen Open Decay to hear the wash, or shorten Closed Decay for a tighter tick.

panels.name: Ring Hats: Open And Closed Groove

controls.text: Ring Hats: Open And Closed Groove

preset.description: Fast sixteenths with accents give a shimmering, rolling hat line. Raise Tone for a thinner, brighter sound or lower it for a darker one.
Only open hats with a very long Open Decay ring over a slow groove and a reverb. Pull Open Decay down to get back to a short sizzle.
Two hats tuned a fourth apart interlock like a high and a low metal pair. Move each Tune to change the character from tinny to dark.
A lazy hat pattern with an LFO sweeping Tone, with a delay behind it. Change the Closed Decay for a looser or snappier feel.
A very low Tune and a long Decay make a round sub kick that rings into the next hit, with a soft hat on top. Push Decay up or Tone down and watch the thump turn into a long boom.

patches.name: Ring Kick: Four On The Floor

preset.description: A tight, punchy kick on every beat with off-beat open hats and a clap on two and four. A slow Movement LFO sweeps the kick's Tone; also try Sweep for more or less pitch drop.

panels.name: Ring Kick: Four On The Floor

controls.text: Ring Kick: Four On The Floor

preset.description: Drive adds a gritty edge and a hard Tone makes the kick cut through a broken-beat groove. An LFO breathes the Drive up and down; try setting it to zero for the clean version.
Three Ring Kicks at different Tunes play a bass-drum line like a bass instrument: low, middle and high notes of the same family. Change the Tune knobs to retune the whole line.
A sparse kick with a soft Tone is thrown into a feedback delay and a roomy reverb, so every hit leaves a trail. Change the delay Feedback or the kick's Decay to fill or empty the space.
A rim shot on the backbeat in place of a snare, over a soft kick and hat. Tune moves the pitch up or down by an octave.
Voice on Clave plays a five-hit son pattern over a steady pulse. Try Rim for a different tone, and Decay for longer or drier hits.
Two rims tuned a fifth apart answer each other like a pair of woodblocks. Use the two Tune knobs to find other intervals.
A long Decay lets each rim ring out like a struck metal tube, then a big reverb carries it away. Shorten Decay to hear the click inside the ring.
An LFO slowly wobbles the rim's Tune over a driving groove so every hit is a slightly different pitch. Try turning the LFO off by lowering Tune modulation or play the pitch by hand.
A plain two-and-four snare with a kick and closed hats. Turn Snappy up for more rattle, down for more drum, and Tone to change how much of the second head you hear.

Soft ghost notes between hard backbeats show how the snare follows velocity: quiet hits are mostly the heads, loud ones add the noise burst. Shorten Decay and raise Snappy for a tighter, drier funk snare.
Tune down low and Decay long give a fat, heavy snare that blooms in a big room. Raise Tune for a tighter pop, or lower Snappy to hear the bare heads.
Sixteenth-note snare rolls get tighter and brighter as an LFO raises Tune over four bars, a classic build to the drop. Try slowing the LFO or lowering Decay to change how the roll connects.
A high-tuned, very short snare turns into a crisp electro tick against a bouncy kick pattern. Raise Tone to make it ring more like a drum and less like a click.
Three toms from low to high roll around the kit over a steady kick and snare. Retune each with Tune; more Bend gives each hit a longer dive.
High Tune, short Decay and almost no Bend make a hand-drum pair. Raise Noise for more slap, or lower Tune for a bigger drum.
A huge slow floor tom with lots of Bend and a long Decay carries a tribal pulse. Bend sets how far the pitch falls on each hit; try pulling it to zero.
Full Bend and no Noise turn the toms into pitch-diving electronic zaps. An LFO moves the Bend amount; try more or less Noise to put the drum back in.
Four toms tuned to a pentatonic scale play a pattern that sounds like a marimba made of drums. Retune any of them with Tune to change the scale.

Four overlapping chords drawn on a four-bar roll play a Voice Cell as a pad, while the Low Pitch and Low Gate outputs pick out the lowest note of each chord for a bass. Open the roll and drag a note to change a chord.

Slot 1 is a steady eighth-note arp, slot 2 an offbeat line with a few extra notes. A slow LFO turns Morph so the arp bends note by note into the other pattern and back; the spare notes fade in and out. Set Morph by hand to freeze a blend.

Every note of this two-bar line has its own ratchet count and chance, so some notes split into quick repeats and others play only now and then. Seed changes which ones sound; Humanise adds a loose feel.

One pattern with a bass line, a lead above it and a long held note between: the Low outputs play a bass voice and the High outputs a lead, while Notes plays a soft pad with all of it. Move a note across and it changes hands.

Long overlapping notes make an eight-bar drone chord progression, and a few quiet notes with ratchets and a chance of sounding sparkle on top. Everything starts a little apart thanks to Humanise. Draw a note to add your own.

A slow stepped LFO turns Rotate, so the same set of divisions moves from output to output: the part that was the kick becomes the hats, then the clap, and the groove reshapes every few bars. Turn Rotate by hand to hear one fixed arrangement, or set Rotate Sync to Next Bar to move on the downbeat.

The Primes set (2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13 and on) rings eight soft bell tones, each on its own division, so they only coincide rarely and the texture keeps shifting. Change Rotate to give each bell a different, slower or faster clock without touching the tuning.

patches.name: Rotating Div: Powers of Two Groove

preset.description: With the Powers of 2 set (1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32...) every output lands on a regular beat, giving a tidy four-to-the-floor skeleton of kick, claps and hats. Raise Rotate by one and each part jumps to the next division for an instant half-time or double-time feel.

panels.name: Rotating Div: Powers of Two Groove

controls.text: Rotating Div: Powers of Two Groove

preset.description: The Stair output reads all eight gates as one binary number, a jumpy staircase that repeats with the pattern, and a Quantizer snaps it to a scale so the Fibonacci set (1, 2, 3, 5, 8...) writes a melody. Change the Quantizer's Scale, or Rotate, for a different tune from the same clocks.

In Extend mode, Rotate does not wrap around the set but continues it, so with the Evens set each turn of the knob brings in longer divisions (2, 4, 6... then 18, 20 and beyond). A slow sawtooth LFO turns Rotate up through the bars, thinning the hats and claps out as it climbs.

One bar of claves, castanets and granite blocks is cut into sixteen equal slices. With Slice Mode on, each key plays one slice (slice 1 on the Root Note), so a step sequencer re-orders the bar into a new groove; two slices are set to Reverse in the view. Edit the sequence, drag a marker, or select a slice to change its pitch and level.

Two recorded piano notes, C3 and C4, each sit on their own Sampler with the right Root Note, and a step sequencer plays the left hand on one and the right hand on the other. Sampler pitches the single recording across the keyboard, tape-style. Try Quality for cleaner pitch shifting, Release for staccato, or Cutoff for a softer touch.

A Thai gong played in Layers voice mode: every note starts three playheads a fifth apart (Layer Pitch 7), each a little later than the last, so one gong becomes a bell cluster. Slow notes ring into each other. Change Layers, Layer Pitch or Layer Offset for other stacks, or switch Voice Mode back to Poly for a single gong.

A short, steady stretch of a tam-tam recording is looped (Mode Loop with a crossfade that hides the seam) and played slowly from the keys as a shimmering metallic pad. A slow LFO scrubs the Position inside the region and another opens the filter. Move Start and End to choose a different part of the gong, or shorten the region for a more electronic drone.

A tambourine shake is cut into four slices, all in choke group 1, so each new hit cuts off the one before it. Trigger By is CV: a trigger starts a playhead and a random control signal on the Slice input picks which part of the shake plays, one of them reversed. Change the sequence, or select a slice in the view and give it another group.

A thin sine-and-triangle melody gains harmonics from the Tube curve at moderate Drive: rounder, fuller and gently compressed. Raise Drive to move from warmth to overdrive, or compare with the Tape and Diode characters.

A shuffled beat runs through the Tape curve with some Sag and Age: the peaks soften, the highs round off and the kit glues together. Raise Age for a worn, uneven machine or Drive for heavier compression.
A saw lead hits the Diode curve hard, with Color tilted toward the highs: a bright, snarling edge that stays musical. Pull Color negative for a darker growl, or lower Drive for a cleaner sound.

A slow LFO moves Bias on a soft sine pad, so the curve becomes lopsided and even harmonics come and go: the tone drifts between hollow, nasal and full. Change the cable amount to wander more, or switch Character.

Bass and a sparse beat go through heavy Sag and Age on the Tape curve: the level sags on loud hits and the sound slowly drifts like a tired old machine. Turn Sag and Age to zero to hear the clean, steady version.

The Scene output drives the Drum Grid's Pattern input: intro, groove, fill and break are four patterns, played in the order intro, groove x2, fill, groove x2, break by the arranger's play order. Change Repeat or Slot knobs to rewrite the song; the Cycle trigger marks each time round.

Scene 2 is the groove and holds on a Chance follow action: each time round there is a one in three chance of jumping to the fill scene, otherwise it plays on. The fill always returns to the groove. Raise Chance 2 for busier fills, or change the Seed for another sequence.

Four scenes of four bars bring layers in and out through the lane gates: the pad from the start, the bass from scene 2, the lead from scene 3 and the bells only in scene 4. Edit a lane's From and To to rearrange who plays when.

Six scenes that all follow Random: the arranger wanders between them and each scene's lane fires a trigger into its own bell tone, so the tune is a random walk that repeats exactly while the Seed stays put. Change the Seed for a new walk or the Scene Length for a faster one.

Eight scenes of one bar each, and the linear Scene output climbs a staircase that opens a low-pass filter on the arp; the Cycle trigger plays a clap when the staircase starts again. Change Scenes to shorten the climb or Follow on a scene to Previous to make it zigzag.

Five segments draw an envelope no ADSR can: a quick rise, a dip, a second slower swell and a long fade, and every note of the tune follows that shape. Change a segment's Level or Time and hear the hump move.

Set to run freely, the chain of four segments repeats like an LFO with a shape you choose: a fast ramp up, a step, a hold and a slide back. It sweeps the filter on a plucked arpeggio; stretch Time Scale or change the Shape knobs to reshape the sweep.

Eight segments alternate between a tiny rise and a fall to zero, each bounce shorter and quieter than the last, so one gate rings out as a dropped ball. Move the Level of a segment to change how high it bounces.

A free-running chain of four equal segments hands out a gate at each step, and those gates play a kick, hat, snare and hat: the segments are the sequencer. Change a segment's Time to shift the groove, or raise Count to add steps.

One three-segment shape (rise, hold while the key is down, fall) opens the filter on a pad while its inverted output fades a noise wash down, so the sound turns from airy to tonal and back with every chord. Try Release set to Jump to cut the swell short when the chord ends.
Every note triggers a one-shot shape from the library, a soft 1:8 pluck, that opens both volume and filter. Try the other plucks, Bounce and Echoes shapes, or move Morph to change its curve.

In Loop mode the Wobble shape repeats once per beat and swings the cutoff of a held bass, locked to the tempo. Switch Sync to another note length for faster or slower wobble, or try Double wobble and Swing wobble.

A pad is held steady while one looped Shape Env breathes its volume over two bars and a second one slowly sways its filter over four. Choose Heartbeat or Sway shapes, or change Sync, and the whole pad takes on a new pulse.

The rhythm shapes are patterns drawn as amplitude: one looping shape chops a held chord into syncopated stabs, another carves a bass note into a different pattern. Pick any of the x.xx shapes, or change Sync, to make a new groove.

With Reverse on, a plucked shape plays backwards: each note swells up and is cut off at its peak, like a tape played in reverse. Switch Reverse off for normal plucks, or lengthen Time for slower swells.

Lock at its top position freezes the register, so its eight bits recycle forever as a fixed little melody in D minor pentatonic over two octaves. Change the seed or Length to get a different tune; Length 5 or 7 against the drums makes the melody drift against the beat.

Lock sits just below frozen, so now and then a bit flips and the melody changes by a note or two instead of repeating exactly. A slow LFO nudges Lock between nearly frozen and quite loose; turn it down to hear the tune stay put, up to hear it wander.

As the bits travel along the register, each bit output plays the same rhythm one step later than the one before, so a kick, snare, hat and clap echo one rhythm in canon. Change Length to reshape the pattern for all four at once, or Lock below the top to let it mutate.

patches.name: Shift Register: Bits from a Data Input

preset.description: Source is set to Data, so the register is fed from a gate patched into its Data input, here a pair of square LFOs with different speeds mixed together. The register turns that slow on-off pattern into a lively stepped melody. Switch Source to Data ⊕ Loop to blend the old loop with the new input.

panels.name: Shift Register: Bits from a Data Input

controls.text: Shift Register: Bits from a Data Input

preset.description: The Mix output adds the bits up with the Weight knobs, here as a stepped voltage that sweeps the cutoff of a filter on a held saw bass, while Voltage plays the pitches. Change Weight 1 to 3 to reshape the sweep, or set a weight negative to flip it.

In Loop mode six slopes breathe at related rates, and each one swells a different note of a chord, so the harmony slowly rearranges itself. Move Harmonics to change how far apart the rates are and Skew to shift each swell between rise and fall.

One trigger starts all six slopes in AR mode; with Harmonics up, the higher slopes die away faster, so each note sparkles then settles into its lower partials. Move Harmonics down for a darker, longer ring or change Rate to stretch the whole decay.

In Sound mode the slopes run at audio rate and follow the sequencer's pitch, so the Six Slopes is the oscillator itself; the Sum output is a rich, buzzy tone. Try Snap on Integer or Just for harmonic spacing, or Curve and Skew for different timbres.

Sync ties the Loop mode to the tempo and Snap on Integer keeps every rate an exact multiple, so six slopes move filter, tone, pulse and volume in polyrhythm that never drifts. Change Sync or Harmonics and listen to the grooves reshuffle.

In ASR mode each of six slopes rises while a gate is held and falls when it ends; with Harmonics below zero the lower notes of the chord arrive first and the top ones drift in last. Change Harmonics, Rate or the sequencer's gate length to alter the unfolding.

patches.name: Spectral Blend: Drums Wear a Pad

preset.description: A drum loop in A and a sustained minor chord in B: it keeps the pad's colour while every hit chops it into the beat's spectral shape. Swap Magnitude and Phase (0/1 against 1/0) to hear which sound lends the rhythm and which the tone.

panels.name: Spectral Blend: Drums Wear a Pad

controls.text: Spectral Blend: Drums Wear a Pad

patches.name: Spectral Blend: Bass Below, Arp Above

preset.description: A bass line in A and a bright arpeggio in B are joined at a pivot frequency: with Tilt up, the lows come from the bass and the highs from the arp, so one sound seems to play both. A slow LFO moves the Pivot up and down; try a Tilt of -1 to turn the roles around.

panels.name: Spectral Blend: Bass Below, Arp Above

controls.text: Spectral Blend: Bass Below, Arp Above

preset.description: A pluck melody runs through Spectral Blend while a gate from a clock divider freezes the spectrum on every other bar, turning a single note into a long drone under the live line. Change the divider for shorter or longer holds, or add Blur to soften the frozen chord.

patches.name: Spectral Blend: Partials Come and Go

preset.description: A drum loop goes into In A alone, and the spectral gate removes every frequency bin below a threshold while Smear leaves a spectral afterglow; a slow LFO on the mid gate lets partials appear and vanish. Raise Smear for a bigger wash or turn on Invert Gate to keep only what is quiet.

panels.name: Spectral Blend: Partials Come and Go

controls.text: Spectral Blend: Partials Come and Go

preset.description: Two different melodies, a soft sine line in A and a buzzy saw line in B, are morphed in the geometric law, where a partial only one of them has stays quiet halfway, so the change is smooth. Slow random values move Magnitude and Phase; try Linear for a cruder cross-fade.

A plucked phrase is recorded onto the reel for two bars, then the splice loops it back with Sync on 2 bars, so the loop stays on the beat. The live phrase is heard while it is recorded (Monitor). Try Sync, Speed or Window Size to bend the loop, or set Record Target to Current splice and Overdub to layer more on top.

A drum bar is recorded, then plays from the reel while a ramp pulls Speed down towards zero every two bars: the whole loop slows, drops in pitch and winds to a halt before the tape snaps back to full speed. Edit the ramp's Rate or amount, or try a negative Speed to run the tape backwards.

One recorded note is replayed as an instrument: a sequencer's Pitch drives the Speed input (1 V per octave) and its trigger restarts the splice, with Loop on One-shot. Change the sequence for a new tune, or Window Size for another timbre; pitch and speed move together, like tape.

A drum bar is recorded and then replayed one eighth at a time: Window Size is 1/8 of the splice and a stepped random source picks Position every eighth note, so the break is re-cut into a stuttering new beat. The random loops after eight steps, so the pattern repeats; raise Loop towards 0 for endless variation.

A short chord arpeggio is recorded, then replayed in 3 % windows with Overlap at 90 %, which turns it into a granular cloud; a slow LFO scrubs Position across the splice. Raise Window Size to hear the phrase re-emerge, or lower Overlap below 30 % for a rhythmic stutter.

Each stage holds its note for a different number of pulses, from one to six, so a slow pad-like line in Eb Lydian lingers on some notes and moves quickly past others. Change a stage's Pulses in the view to stretch or squeeze the phrase.

Eight stages that each use a different gate mode: a single First hit, notes that repeat on Every pulse, a long Hold, a Ratchet burst and a Rest, so one riff shows all the ways a stage can fire. Click a stage's gate mode in the view to change it.

Stages marked Slide glide into the next pitch over the Slide Time, and the accented stages fire an extra gate that snaps the filter open, giving a squelchy bass over a four-on-the-floor beat. Raise Slide Time for slower glides or Accent for a harder bite.

Twelve stages are played in Pendulum mode: forward to the last stage and back again, with the Phrase length marking the repeat. Switch Mode to Forward, Reverse, Random or Brownian to hear the same stages in other orders.

In Brownian mode the playhead takes a random step to a neighbouring stage each time, so a Dorian melody wanders without jumping, and the Stage Start output ticks a hat on every new stage. Change Seed to take another walk, or Stages to widen the range.

Sixteen steps of C major pentatonic, with rests and a few quieter steps, played as short plucks: every note you edit snaps to the scale. Try Scale, Root or Length to reshape the tune, or Gate Length to go from staccato to legato.

A bass line with tied steps, which hold the previous pitch into the next step so the notes run together, and a little Swing for a rolling feel, over a four-on-the-floor beat. Try more Swing, or shorten Gate Length to hear the ties disappear.

Twelve steps of D Dorian run forward and then backward, in triplet eighths, so the bell line rises and falls without repeating the end notes. Switch Direction to Forward, Backward or Random, or change Length to move the turning points.

Variation is set to about half, so around every other step may jump up to a fifth away from its programmed note, and a slow LFO swells and fades that chance. Change Var. Range for bigger leaps, or Seed to deal a different set of surprises.

A second, slow Step Sequencer walks a four-bar progression and its Pitch goes into the first one's Transpose input, so the same eight-step figure is carried to a new root each bar. The slow one also plays the sub bass. Edit either sequence to change the harmony or the figure.

A plucked loop is recorded into a four second rolling tape and played back four times slower by the Smear engine, so the notes melt into a slowly changing pad over a plain beat. Try Stretch at 8 for a still drone, Wobble for a drifting sense of time, or Mix lower to hear the live melody under the pad.

An arpeggio is cut into 250 ms grains that are scattered around the play head, four at a time, while the head crawls through a four second tape at a quarter of the speed. The result is a shimmering cloud with the dry arpeggio underneath. Move Scatter between 0 and 100 %, shorten Grain for a glitchier texture, or raise Pitch.

A short chord progression is recorded once, then the tape is frozen and Position Mode is set to Scrub, so a slow LFO on Position sweeps a spectral scanner back and forth through the chords. It sounds like one sustained organ whose harmony slides between the recorded chords. Change the LFO rate, or turn Freeze off to hear the tape move again.

Hold Range loops a window of only 4 % of a one-bar tape, which stutters a bright pluck line into a tiny repeating loop. A slow random source moves Start, so the stutter keeps landing on a different piece of the phrase. Change Range for longer or shorter loops, or Grains for a rougher edge.

A drum and bass loop is replayed from a rolling tape seven semitones up while Wobble with a random shape keeps changing the stretch factor, so the groove slows down, speeds up and smears as if time itself was swaying. Turn Wobble down for a steady pitch-shifted copy, or set Pitch to -12 for a heavy, slowed sound.

A slow LFO moves Spread between 0 and 100 %: the eight oscillators sit on the root, then leave it one after another and slide up into a minor ninth stack, and fold back again. Glide sets how lazily they move. Try Chord, Count and Width, or press Reshuffle for a new set of glide times.

With Spread at 0 every oscillator plays the same note, so the swarm becomes a fat unison lead: seven bright saws, Detune in a Fan pattern, a little Width. A filter envelope closes after each note. Raise Spread a touch to hear the lead turn into a chord, or change Pattern to Alternate or Outer.

Set to a whole scale instead of a chord: sixteen oscillators across four octaves of Hirajoshi, fully spread, with high Drift and Width so the notes shimmer and wander. Soft sine-like Warp keeps it glassy. Change Chord to another scale, lower Range for a narrower cloud, or sweep Drift by hand.

Cross FM pushes each oscillator's phase with its neighbour's, turning a Cluster chord into dense, bell-like metal. A trigger at the start of every bar reshuffles the detune pattern and glide times, so each bar is a new cloud, and an envelope on every beat strikes it. Lower Cross FM for gritty chords, or raise it for noise.

Swarm's Root output is a clean anchor and Upper carries only the oscillators above the root octave. Here the Root goes through a low-pass for the bassline, while Upper is filtered brighter and swept by an LFO for the chord. Use two different filters, or one effect on only one of them.

A saw tone climbs from 80 Hz to 6 kHz over eight bars while its Sweep output opens a filter on a bed of noise; at the top, the End trigger fires a crash. Edit Start, Stop and Sweep Sync for a shorter or lower riser, or switch Law to Lin to hear it rush through the bass.

A triangle wave glides up and down between 300 Hz and 1.2 kHz, two bars each way, on a linear law like an old air-raid horn, with Drift keeping the pitch slightly alive. Change Direction, Waveform or Retrace to turn the siren into a whooping alarm, and let the delay ring behind it.

In Burst mode the tone is silent until a trigger, and each trigger plays three clean cycles at the frequency the sweep has reached, so a steady sixteenth pulse becomes blips that climb through the band and start over every two bars. Raise Burst Count for longer blips, or change Stop to widen the climb.

A slow sweep from 100 Hz to 8 kHz crosses three Markers, and each crossing, in both directions, fires a kick and a hat, while the End trigger calls the snare once per cycle. Move a Marker to shift the rhythm, change Sweep Sync for a faster or slower pulse, or set Markers to 1 for a sparse beat.

In Triggered mode each sequencer note fires one quick downward sweep that begins on its own pitch (the Pitch input), so a bassline of zaps shoots across the speakers. Change Sweep Time for longer or shorter zaps, Waveform for a different edge, or Direction to make them rise.

The same riff is played by four different oscillators, and the Switch hands the output to the next one every half note with a short crossfade: saw, hollow pulse, triangle and a bright octave. Change Direction to Ping-Pong or Random, or lengthen Fade to blend the voices.

Four sustained layers, a soft pad, a breathy noise band, a deep sine and a shimmering high chord, are slowly crossfaded by the Switch in Random Walk order, one step at a time, so the texture wanders without ever jumping. Change Seed for another route.

Used the other way round, one input goes to eight outputs: a single riff is sent to a dry output, an echo, a high-pass filter and a huge reverb in turn, each for half a bar. Try Direction Random or Length 2 to make it jump between only two of them.

Four sine drones stacked on different chord tones are passed one at a time through the Switch in Glide mode and ping-pong order, with a long Fade so each tone seems to slide into the next. Change Mode to Crossfade for a cleaner blend or Fade for a quicker move.

One drum pattern plays four different drums at once, but the Switch lets only one of them through, stepping to the next each bar by a trigger: the same groove turns from kick to snare to clap to tom. Lengthen the Length setting to add silent bars, or change Direction.

A lamp-stabilised sine on its own: it warms up, bounces slightly in level and carries a faint mains hum, a slowly breathing drone in a big room. Raise Drift for more wander, or change Mains to Off for a perfectly clean tone.

With Loop Gain below 100 % the oscillator dies away on its own, and a trigger on Kick makes it ring like a struck tuning fork. Change Loop Gain for longer or shorter rings, and Kick for how hard it is hit.
A plain sine melody from the Test Oscillator's Pitch input with a short envelope, about as clean a tone as exists. Add Fm from the LFO for vibrato or raise Drift to hear a warmer, wobblier note.
The square output at the lowest range plays a rounded bass line through a low-pass filter, over a simple beat. Change Range to jump the whole line by decades or move Freq for a different key.
The Lamp output, a slow signal showing the oscillator's amplitude loop breathing, opens a filter on a held chord of Oscillators. Raise Settle for slower swings, or Loop Gain for harder bounces.

On the Slow range the Tidal loops over many seconds and its four outputs trail one another through Phase: the filter opens, the resonance swells and the tone shape drifts, in turn. Move Skew to make the tide rise slowly and fall fast, or switch Relation to Ratio.

With Range on Audio and the sequencer's pitch patched in, the Tidal becomes an oscillator: A is the main tone while B, C and D add related shapes. Skew, Curve and Smooth change the waveform, Spread changes how the other outputs differ.

Sync locks the looping Tidal to the beat, so its slopes pulse a bass line in time: A makes the volume duck and bounce, B opens the filter on the off-beats. Change Sync or Skew to move the bounce, or Polarity to flip it.

In AD mode each sequencer gate fires one quick rise-and-fall: A shapes the volume of a bright pluck, while B, with Spread, opens the filter for a vowel-like wah on every note. Increase Frequency to shorten the whole shape or Skew to move its peak.

In AR mode a held gate makes the Tidal rise, and when it finishes falling its End output fires a snare: a pad swells in, fades, and the drum answers. Change Frequency to stretch the swell, or Skew to move where it peaks.

The Transport's Playing output is high whenever the song runs, and here it opens an envelope that slowly fades in a warm pad under a beat, then lets it ring out when you press Stop. Move the Tempo knob to change the speed of everything, or press Stop and Play to hear the pad breathe in and out.

The Tempo output carries the speed as a control value (BPM divided by 100) and here it also sets the cutoff of a filter on an arpeggio, so a faster song is automatically a brighter one. Drag the Tempo knob up and down and listen to the tone follow the speed.

A very slow LFO is patched into the Tempo knob, so the whole song speeds up and slows down by a few BPM over about a minute like a band pushing and pulling. Lower the cable amount on the LFO, or unpatch it to hold the tempo steady.

MIDI Clock Out is switched on, so while this groove plays the Transport also sends clock, start and stop to a connected MIDI Out, keeping outboard gear in time with it. You will hear a driving bass line over a four-on-the-floor kick; use Tap to set the tempo.

Link is switched on, so this song shares its tempo and start with any other Link-enabled app on the network, while a dreamy arpeggio and a soft beat play. Turn Link off to go solo, or use MIDI Clock In to follow a drum machine instead.

A pure tone drifts slowly sharp and flat of a note; each time it slides through the In Tune window the Tuner's gate strikes a soft bell, so you can hear the moment it is right. Widen In Tune for more bells per sweep, or narrow it to catch only the exact centre.

Two saw voices a fifth apart share a pad; the upper one wanders in pitch and the Tuner's Cents output pans it and opens a filter, so how sharp or flat it is becomes the movement. Try a wider Damping for lazier motion, or invert the cable amounts.

A drone pair floats in pitch, and whenever one voice passes through tune the Tuner strikes a mallet voice that plays the note it is hearing, a fifth up, into a long reverb. Change Reference A to shift where the chime lands, or raise In Tune for a busier shimmer.

A pluck line slowly slips out of tune and back; the Tuner follows its pitch and re-pitches a second voice an octave up, which only sounds while the line is in tune. Make In Tune smaller for shorter, rarer answers, or shorten Damping for a quicker tracker.

A melody is played a semitone low, and the Tuner's Reference A is set to 415 so it reads each note as exactly in tune, ticking a hi-hat on every sure note. Move Reference A away from 415 and the ticks stop; at 440 the whole line reads flat.

The two fluctuating curves wander at unrelated speeds: one opens and closes the filter on a plucked line, the other changes the tone shape. Raise F1 Rate and F2 Rate to speed them up, or lower F1 Spread to shrink the sweep.

Quantized outputs jump between a few evenly spaced levels (Q1 Bits sets how many): Q1 pushes the pitch up by octaves and Q2 moves the filter, both in time with the eighth notes. Try Q1 Interval at 7 st for stacked fifths or raise the bits for more levels.

Each note of the line tells the Store input to take a fresh stored value, which then holds until the next note; it sets the filter, and the Store Trigger output also fires a hi-hat. Raise Correlation so each value leans on the last, or move Distribution to favour low or high settings.

The Integrated output is the running total of the stored steps, so it wanders like a slow random walk; here it steers the brightness of a held pad and the stored value tilts the oscillators. Change Integrate to make the walk shorter-lived or longer, and Store Rate for how often it is nudged.

Setting Shape to Edges makes the random values favour the extremes, so the filter on this bass line jumps between very closed and wide open instead of sitting in the middle. Switch Shape to Bell or Uniform to hear it settle.

A slow triangle LFO is sampled by an eighth-note clock in Sample & Hold mode, and the stepped result is snapped to a scale to play the oscillator: a tune that never repeats. Change the LFO rate for a different walk, or pick another Mode to hear the raw values.

The sequencer's pitch passes through the Utility's Slew before it reaches the oscillator, so every leap turns into a slide. Turn Slew down for sharp steps, or up until the notes smear into one long wail.

Two slow LFOs are added in the Utility and together they swing past plus and minus one, where Fold reflects them back, so the filter on the arpeggio keeps turning around at new places. Switch Mode to Through to hear the same sweeps without the folds.

A slow triangle plus a fast sine run through the Utility, and its Gate output goes high whenever the sum rises above Threshold: the ripples cross the line in bursts and trigger the claps. Move Threshold to make the claps sparse or dense.

A sine LFO into Rectify mode flips its negative half upwards, so the pad's volume pulses at twice the LFO speed, always rising from silence. Change the LFO rate for a slow pulse or a fast shimmer, or switch Mode to Through for a plain tremolo.

A saw note shaped by a short envelope into the VCA's Gain, with Response on Exponential so the decay sounds natural and plucked. Switch Response to Linear to hear a stiffer, more abrupt tail, or change the envelope's Decay.

A held chord goes through a VCA whose Gain rests at a middle value while a triangle LFO swings it up and down, a classic tremolo. Raise the LFO Rate for a flutter, change its amount for a deeper chop, or move the VCA's Gain to rebalance.

A very slow attack on the envelope lets a rich pad fade in and out through a VCA with Response set to Linear, so the volume rises evenly instead of rushing in at the end. Compare it with Exponential, or lengthen Attack and Release.

Every kick fires an envelope that pushes the pad VCA's Gain down by a negative amount, so the chords dip on the beat and swell back between hits. Change the envelope Release for a longer pump, or raise the VCA's Gain for an even bigger pad.

A sustained saw chord is chopped into a rhythm by a drum-grid track that fires a tight envelope into the VCA's Gain, the stuttering gate used in trance and electro. Edit the pattern, or lengthen the envelope Release to soften the chops.

A low saw drone has many partials; the analyzer is a very narrow band-pass that an LFO moves slowly over them, so you hear single sine-like overtones appear and fade, over the dry drone. Change Bandwidth for a wider or glassier peak, or move Frequency by hand.

Mode is Sweep: the narrow band glides from low to high and back across a bed of noise and drums, drawing out a rising and falling whistle. Change Sweep Dir, Span or Sweep Time, or widen Bandwidth for a softer tone.

In Lock mode the analyzer finds the strongest partial of a melody and its Track output drives a pure sine that shadows every note an octave up. Change Listen to move the range it hears, or Threshold to make it more or less eager to lock.

The analyzer is tuned to the kick's low note and its Level output follows how strong that partial is; the level swells a chord pad in time with the beat. Move Frequency to follow a different drum, or Gain to make the pad react more.

A wide band-pass picks the fundamental of a plucked line and the Shifted output moves it up by the Capture amount, a seventh semitones for a fifth, so a thin sine harmony chases each note. Change Capture for other intervals, or Bandwidth to let more of the original through.

An external saw riff enters the Folder's input and an LFO moves Fold up and down, so each note folds back on itself into a growl that opens and closes. Change Symmetry for a hollower tone or lower Tap for a gentler fold.

With Source on Internal the Folder is its own voice: a slow sequencer sets the pitch, Wave and Fold drift under two LFOs, and a plain sine turns into a shifting, metallic drone. Try Coarse and Fine for beating pairs of partials.

A low note from the internal sine is pushed off-centre with Symmetry and folded at Tap 3, giving a bass with strong even harmonics and a nasal, vocal edge. Change Symmetry to the other side or raise Fold for a buzzier note.

A slow pad goes through the Folder with Spread turned up, so the left and right channels fold by different amounts and the pad opens into a wide, shimmering stereo image. Pull Spread down to bring it back to the centre.

A drum beat passes through the Folder at half Mix: the kick gains a hard, clicky harmonic edge and the hats shimmer, while the dry hits keep their weight. Raise Fold or Mix for a more broken, industrial kit.

A slow LFO scans through the Analog bank, so the tone evolves from soft to sharp and back across a pentatonic line. Change Bank for a different family of tables, or set Scan by hand to pick one spot in the grid.
The Vowel bank with X and Y wandering under two slow LFOs: the pad seems to murmur through different mouth shapes. Try Frame Blend on Step for abrupt vowel changes instead of smooth morphs.

With Path set to Spiral, one Scan knob walks the whole 8 by 8 grid in a spiral, and an envelope on Scan sweeps it for every note: each pluck travels through many tables. Try Rows, Snake or Diagonal for other journeys through the grid.

The Bell bank played softly and slowly, with Y raised a little by each note's envelope, gives glassy, inharmonic chimes. Change X to pick other bells from the grid, or Read to Linear for a rougher, more digital edge.

A low sequence on the Fold bank with Warp Mode on Sync and a slow LFO on Warp, plus a little Sub Level, for a bass that snarls and calms over a beat. Switch Warp Mode to Mirror, Squash or Steps for other kinds of damage.

A lead line plays while the Wheel sits at rest in the middle (zero) and feeds the sequencer's Transpose input at a small amount: push it up or down and the whole line bends by a couple of notes, then springs back when you let go. Turn Spring off to leave it where you put it.

Min is 0 and Spring is off, so this Wheel behaves like a mod wheel that stays where you leave it: it raises the wavefolder inside a dual oscillator, turning a plain tone into a bright, buzzing one. Drag it slowly across the tune and listen to the overtones appear.

The Wheel rides the Drive and bit depth of a Crunch effect on a whole beat and bass: at rest the groove is clean and warm, pushed up it breaks into grit. Min is 0 here, so the wheel only adds grit; set it to -1 and the lower half takes the drive below the starting point.

A chord-like arpeggio passes through a slow phaser whose Centre frequency is steered by the Wheel instead of its LFO: roll it up and the notches climb, down and they sink. Raise the phaser's Feedback to make the sweep more vocal.

The Wheel pushes the delay time of a tape-style echo while a pluck melody plays: nudge it and the echoes slide in pitch as the tape speeds up or slows down, then settle when the wheel springs home. Turn Smooth up for lazier moves.

One random stream, three ways: Stepped jumps the filter, Smooth glides the tone and Wobble overshoots and rings on the reverb. All three follow the same underlying values, so they feel related. Change Smooth and Wobble on the module to reshape the glides and overshoots.

With Wobble high, every jump of the random value overshoots and rings before it settles, so the filter on this held chord seems to bounce. Reduce Wobble for a plain glide, or increase Chaos for a more unstable movement.

The Burst output fires a quick run of triggers every so often: here they flutter a hi-hat and clap while the clock output keeps the kick steady. Raise Burst for more frequent runs, and change Burst Size for longer flutters.

The Stepped output goes through a Quantizer to become a melody in a scale, and the Compare output decides when a note plays, so both pitch and rhythm are random but musical. Raise Wobble's Rate for a busier tune or change the Quantizer's Scale.

A triangle LFO patched into Sample is read at each tick of the Wobble clock, and the Stepped output holds the value in between: a classic sample-and-hold filter pattern that stays related to the LFO. Change the LFO rate or the Wobble Sync to change the pattern.

The pad's X axis drives the cutoff and its Y axis the resonance of a saw bass, so dragging across the pad goes from dull to bright and up from smooth to squelchy. Drag the dot around while the groove runs.

X sets how much echo you hear and Y how many repeats it feeds back on a bell melody, so the bottom left is dry and the top right is a cloud of repeating notes. Try dragging along the edges to change only one thing at a time.

X morphs the oscillator through its waveforms and Y changes its pulse width, so each corner of the pad is a different voice for the same slow tune. Park the dot in a corner or move it while the notes sound.

X controls the sequencer's Variation, the chance that notes are shifted away from the programmed ones, and Y its Gate Length, so you can shake up the tune and make it shorter or smoother at the same time. Park the pad low-left for the plain tune.
Min and Max are set to -1 and +1, so the pad's centre is zero: X bends the pitch a little either way and Y pushes the filter above or below its starting point. Narrow Min and Max for gentler moves.

Two sines a fifth apart draw a slow-turning knot on the scope; each time the pattern stands still enough, the Still gate fires a bell. Change Still Tolerance to Loose and the bells come more often, or tune the Y oscillator by ear to lock them.

A pad's left and right channels go into X and Y, so the scope shows the stereo image: a diagonal line means near-mono, a round cloud means wide. The Correlation output opens the reverb when the image narrows. Turn the Chorus's Spread down and watch the cloud pinch.

In Y-T mode the scope is an ordinary oscilloscope: a bass line's waveform stands still on screen, triggered on every rising edge. Shorten Timebase to see single cycles, or turn the Oscillator's Shape and watch the wave change under the sound.

A bell-like FM pair plays a pentatonic line; the carrier goes to X and the modulated tone to Y, so each note draws a tangled knot that unwinds as it decays. Raise the Oscillator's FM Depth for a busier knot, or X Gain to stretch the figure.

patches.name: XY Scope: Ratio Plays a Voice

preset.description: A fixed sine on X and a sweeping sine on Y: the scope measures their ratio and its Ratio output, as a pitch, plays a third voice that follows the interval between them. Change the sweep rate and the follower glides along; try Timebase for a clearer picture.

preset.description: Zone 1 turns the delay into a tuned comb: a drum loop is pushed through it while a sequencer plays its Pitch input, so the beat rings out a melody. Change Feedback for a longer ring, or Zone to leave the comb behind.

Zone 3 in Tape mode with a little Wobble: a plucked line is followed by warm, drifting echoes that darken as they repeat. Raise Wobble and Character for a worn tape, or move Time while it plays to hear the pitch slide.

In the longest zone a square LFO raises Hold every other bar group, so the delay stops listening and loops what it just heard while the live melody plays over it. Change the LFO's Sync, or fire Hold from a Button.

Two square LFOs gate Reverse and Ping-Pong on their own cycles, so the echoes of an arpeggio flip backwards and hop between the speakers in changing combinations. Edit either LFO, or turn Diffuse up to blur the reversals.

Zone 2 with Diffuse and Character turned up blurs a slow chord progression into a soft, slowly shifting wash. Lower Diffuse to bring back distinct echoes, or change Offset to push the left and right times apart.
